artifacts.name: A Day Carved From Rising Winds
artifacts.why: Best in slot. The 2-piece gives +18% Attack. The 4-piece gives +25% Attack after hits, even off-field, and with Witch's Homework completed it also gives +20% CRIT Rate.

artifacts.name: Shimenawa's Reminiscence
artifacts.why: The best general alternative. The 2-piece gives +18% Attack. The 4-piece uses 15 Energy when he casts his Skill to give +50% Normal, Charged and Plunging Damage for 10 seconds. It suits him because he rarely uses his Burst.

artifacts.name: Desert Pavilion Chronicle
artifacts.why: A transitional set. The 2-piece gives +15% Anemo Damage. The 4-piece gives attack speed and +40% Damage after Charged Attack hits, and the rotation must start with a Charged Attack.

artifacts.name: Marechaussee Hunter
artifacts.why: Strong with Furina, but it limits team building.

artifacts.name: Scarlet Proof
artifacts.why: Good in Stellar-Swirl teams, but behind A Day Carved From Rising Winds.

artifacts.name: Gladiator's Finale
artifacts.why: Easy to get and boosts Normal Attacks. Good while you farm A Day Carved From Rising Winds.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: A Day Carved From Rising Winds (Attack +18%) with Gladiator's Finale (Attack +18%)
artifacts.why: A flexible Attack percent mix while you farm the 4-piece set.

builds/varka.name: Varka
builds/varka.source: Several Varka build guides for version 7.1: Icy Veins, GenshinBuilds and KeqingMains. They agree on Gest of the Mighty Wolf, A Day Carved From Rising Winds, Attack percent Sands, a CRIT Damage or CRIT Rate Circlet and Skill as the top talent. They disagree on the Burst (Icy Veins ranks it second, KeqingMains says keep it at level 1) and on the Goblet (Pyro Damage Bonus before C2, then Attack percent). GenshinBuilds' stats and rarity were garbled, so rarity comes from Icy Veins and KeqingMains. Star ratings for Prototype Archaic, Redhorn Stonethresher, Verdict, The Unforged, Wolf's Gravestone, Fang of the Mountain King, Tidal Shadow, Blade of Atonement, Earthshaker and Song of Broken Pines are from my own knowledge. Prune is an Anemo support named by one guide.

stats.circlet: CRIT Damage or CRIT Rate (CRIT Damage is recommended with A Day Carved From Rising Winds)
stats.goblet: Pyro Damage Bonus in a Pyro team before C2, otherwise Attack% (at C2 and above Attack% is about equal, and Anemo Damage Bonus can work)
stats.sands: Attack%
stats.substats: CRIT Rate and CRIT Damage first, then Attack%, then Elemental Mastery. Skip Energy Recharge, since he rarely uses his Burst. Build a little Elemental Mastery only against enemies where Melt or Vaporize helps. Targets: Attack 2,500 to 2,600 (needed to reach the Damage bonus cap), CRIT Rate 80%+, CRIT Damage 160%+.

talents.name: Elemental Skill
talents.why: Top priority. Most of his Damage comes from it, and his Normal and Charged Attacks in Sturm und Drang use the Skill's level.

talents.name: Elemental Burst
talents.why: Usually not worth casting, since it gets no benefit from his passives. Raise his character level to 90 first.

talents.name: Normal Attack
talents.why: Not worth leveling, because its Damage scales with the Skill level.

teams.name: Double Pyro: Prune, Nicole, Durin
teams.note: The best double Pyro team. Venti replaces Prune if she is not C6 or if grouping enemies matters. Nicole gives teamwide Attack and a shield, and Durin shreds Pyro and Anemo RES.

teams.name: Double Pyro: Venti, Bennett, Durin
teams.note: For players without Nicole. Faruzan can replace Venti. Venti's Burst groups enemies and boosts Swirl Damage.

teams.name: Double Pyro: Ifa, Durin, Bennett (SS)
teams.note: Rated SS by one guide. Ifa heals and boosts Swirl, Durin applies Pyro off-field, and Bennett gives an Attack buff and healing.

teams.name: Hydro: Prune, Vodyanitsa, Furina
teams.note: His best Hydro team. Vodyanitsa heals and shreds Hydro RES, and Furina needs that healing to build Fanfare. Mona can replace Furina.

teams.name: Cryo: Prune, Odette, Cryo Traveler
teams.note: His best Cryo team. It uses Stellar-Swirl. Escoffier can replace the Cryo Traveler.

teams.name: Electro: Venti, Iansan, Fischl
teams.note: An Electro option with Fischl as the off-field Damage dealer.

teams.name: Accessible double Pyro: Sucrose, Bennett, Dehya
teams.note: A team for players without Prune. It deals less Damage than the main teams.

weapons.name: Gest of the Mighty Wolf
weapons.why: His signature weapon and best in slot. It has high base Attack and a CRIT Rate substat, plus attack speed. Four Winds' Hymn stacks Damage Bonus, and with a Hexerei teammate it also gives CRIT Damage. It is used in about 58% of showcased builds.

weapons.name: A Thousand Blazing Suns
weapons.why: The second pick. It has very high base Attack and a CRIT stat. After his Skill or Burst it gives CRIT Damage and Attack for 6 seconds. Its Pyro bonus does nothing for him.

weapons.name: Beacon of the Reed Sea
weapons.why: A CRIT Rate option that gives an Attack bonus after his Skill hits and after he takes Damage, even off-field.

weapons.name: Serpent Spine
weapons.why: The best 4-star. It is a Battle Pass weapon, and it is strong at high refinement in teams with Attack buffs. Its passive needs a shielder.

weapons.name: Prototype Archaic
weapons.why: A craftable 4-star with a high Attack percent substat. One guide calls it the best pick if you do not own better weapons.

weapons.name: Blackcliff Slasher
weapons.why: An easy to obtain 4-star with a strong CRIT Damage substat and stacking Attack, best in multi-enemy content.

weapons.name: Redhorn Stonethresher
weapons.why: Gives CRIT Damage and Normal and Charged Attack Damage, but no CRIT Rate.

weapons.name: Verdict
weapons.why: A CRIT Rate option. Its Attack buff needs a Geo teammate.

weapons.name: Talking Stick
weapons.why: CRIT Rate plus a conditional Attack buff that is reliable in teams with a Pyro buffer.

weapons.name: Ultimate Overlord's Mega Magic Sword
weapons.why: An easy to obtain event weapon with high base Attack and a big Attack boost after his Skill. You need the Melusine world quests to unlock its passive.

weapons.name: The Unforged
weapons.why: High Attack percent and base Attack, but no CRIT. Its passive needs a shielder.

weapons.name: Wolf's Gravestone
weapons.why: High Attack and a team Attack buff against low-HP enemies, but no CRIT stats.

weapons.name: Fang of the Mountain King
weapons.why: Gives Elemental Mastery and Swirl Damage. A niche option.

weapons.name: Tidal Shadow
weapons.why: Competes with a low-refinement Serpent Spine in healed, low-Attack teams. Weak otherwise.

weapons.name: Blade of Atonement
weapons.why: Craftable. Only worth it in Stellar-Swirl teams with no healer.

weapons.name: Earthshaker
weapons.why: Craftable. Its passive only works in double Pyro teams.

weapons.name: Song of Broken Pines
weapons.why: Gives Attack and Normal Attack speed, but its Physical Damage Bonus is wasted.

artifacts.name: Long Night's Oath
artifacts.why: Best set per GenshinBuilds, which says it is tailored for on-field combos and sustained DPS. Icy Veins says it deals slightly better damage than Obsidian Codex.

artifacts.name: Obsidian Codex
artifacts.why: More resin-efficient, and its domain suits a wider range of characters, so Icy Veins generally recommends it for most players. It boosts Normal Attack and Skill DMG after consuming Nightsoul points. The two sets deal very similar damage, so pick the domain you want to farm.

artifacts.name: Long Night's Oath (2pc) + Thundering Fury (2pc), or Gladiator's Finale / Resolution of Sojourner (2pc)
artifacts.why: A flexible mix listed by GenshinBuilds: 2pc Long Night's Oath with 2pc Thundering Fury or a 2pc Attack +18% set. Attack +18% sets include Gladiator's Finale, Resolution of Sojourner and Shimenawa's Reminiscence.

artifacts.name: Marechaussee Hunter
artifacts.why: Only pair it with Furina. GenshinBuilds says it underperforms Obsidian Codex.

builds/varesa.name: Varesa
builds/varesa.source: Icy Veins Varesa guide (updated Sep 28, 2025) and GenshinBuilds Varesa page (DPS build). The two sources disagree on talent order and the substat order; both are noted. Star ratings for weapons the sources did not state are from my own knowledge.

stats.circlet: CRIT Rate or CRIT DMG
stats.goblet: Electro DMG Bonus (ATK% is also fine, per Icy Veins)
stats.sands: ATK%
stats.substats: CRIT Rate > CRIT DMG > ATK% > Energy Recharge (Icy Veins; GenshinBuilds' DPS build lists Energy Recharge first). ER target: about 120-130%, depending on the team.

talents.name: Normal Attack
talents.why: 1st priority in both guides, so level it as high as you can. The sources give the order only, not target levels.

talents.name: Elemental Skill
talents.why: 2nd priority per Icy Veins (GenshinBuilds ranks the Burst second and the Skill third). Level it high too, since it generates and spends her Nightsoul.

talents.name: Elemental Burst
talents.why: Last in Icy Veins' order (second per GenshinBuilds). Her normal Burst deals much less damage than her special one, so a medium level is enough. The levels are my reading of the order, not from the guides.

teams.name: Overload: Mavuika, Iansan, Chevreuse
teams.note: Varesa's best team per Icy Veins, and rated SS by GenshinBuilds (Overload Team #1). Mavuika is often stronger as a DPS in her own team or as a support elsewhere, so if you are not using her here, the Xianyun team is generally better.

teams.name: Overload: Bennett, Iansan, Chevreuse
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds (Overload Team #2). Icy Veins lists Bennett or Ororon in the third slot with Mavuika and Chevreuse.

teams.name: Xianyun plunge team
teams.note: Xianyun provides plunge buffs, though not all of Varesa's attacks count as plunging. Furina adds buffs and builds Fanfare easily with help from Xianyun and Iansan.

teams.name: Xianyun plunge team (Ineffa)
teams.note: Same plunge core as above with Ineffa instead of Iansan. Listed by Icy Veins.

teams.name: Xianyun plunge team (Xilonen)
teams.note: Xilonen replaces Furina. Listed by Icy Veins.

teams.name: Overload: Pyro Traveler
teams.note: A Pyro Traveler stands in for Mavuika. Listed by Icy Veins. Iansan is praised for healing, scroll buffs, ATK% and DMG% buffs, and energy.

weapons.name: Vivid Notions
weapons.why: Best in slot per both Icy Veins and GenshinBuilds. It is her signature weapon, with high base ATK and a CRIT DMG substat. Icy Veins says it is a significant damage increase over other 5-star options and outperforms her C1, so it is competitive with C2.

weapons.name: Reliquary of Truth
weapons.why: Ranked 2nd by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT DMG substat. No further reasoning is given.

weapons.name: Kagura's Verity
weapons.why: Ranked 3rd by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT DMG substat. Also listed by Icy Veins as an alternative.

weapons.name: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds
weapons.why: Ranked 4th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT Rate substat. Also listed by Icy Veins as an alternative.

weapons.name: Tome of the Eternal Flow
weapons.why: Ranked 5th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT DMG substat. Also listed by Icy Veins as an alternative.

weapons.name: Surf's Up
weapons.why: Ranked 6th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT DMG substat.

weapons.name: The Widsith
weapons.why: Ranked 10th by GenshinBuilds (noted at R5), with a CRIT DMG substat. Also listed by Icy Veins. A solid choice if you do not own a 5-star.

weapons.name: Sacrificial Jade
weapons.why: Ranked 12th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT Rate substat. Also listed by Icy Veins. A 4-star stat stick.

weapons.name: Cashflow Supervision
weapons.why: Ranked 7th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT Rate substat. Also listed by Icy Veins as an alternative.

weapons.name: Tulaytullah's Remembrance
weapons.why: Ranked 8th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT DMG substat.

weapons.name: Crane's Echoing Call
weapons.why: Ranked 9th by GenshinBuilds, with an ATK% substat.

weapons.name: Skyward Atlas
weapons.why: Ranked 11th by GenshinBuilds, with an ATK% substat.

weapons.name: Solar Pearl
weapons.why: Ranked 13th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT Rate substat.

weapons.name: Blackcliff Agate
weapons.why: Ranked 14th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT DMG substat.

weapons.name: Dawning Frost
weapons.why: Ranked 15th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT DMG substat.

weapons.name: Flowing Purity
weapons.why: Ranked 16th by GenshinBuilds (noted at R5) and listed by Icy Veins. Icy Veins says most options besides Vivid Notions are close "stat sticks" with no major gap between them.

artifacts.name: A Day Carved From Rising Winds
artifacts.why: Best in slot per GenshinBuilds. It is an Attack set, which fits a shield and buff character that scales with Attack.

artifacts.name: Heart of the Furnace
artifacts.why: Best for Stellar-Conduct teams without a Stellar support like Odette. The 2-piece gives 18% Attack. The 4-piece gives 12% Attack for 12 seconds after Stellar Glimmer triggers and boosts nearby members' Stellar Glimmer reaction damage by 50%. The party bonus doesn't stack.

artifacts.name: Noblesse Oblige
artifacts.why: General support set. His Burst gives the whole team 20% Attack for 12 seconds. It doesn't stack with another Noblesse Oblige, so it suits teams where a teammate like Odette already uses Heart of the Furnace.

artifacts.name: Gladiator's Finale (Attack +18%) + Shimenawa's Reminiscence (Attack +18%)
artifacts.why: Budget mix for early builds while you farm a 4-piece set. Both give Attack, which is his main scaling stat.

buildInfo.support: Valeriy gives Mitya or Cyno a long Electro shield and Attack-based buffs in Stellar-Conduct teams, so build Attack and enough Energy Recharge for his Burst.

builds/valeriy.name: Valeriy
builds/valeriy.source: Researched 2026-11-05 from GenshinBuilds (weapons, artifacts, teams, talent order) and u7buy (weapon stats, artifacts, targets, teams). Valeriy debuted in Version 7.2 on November 4, 2026, so rankings may change after live testing. The two guides disagree on the best artifact set, on Sands, and on talent order, so both views are listed. Icy Veins, GameWith and Fandom were not reachable for him. No 3-star weapon is named in the sources. Re-checked 2026-11-07: GenshinBuilds (v7.2) now lists Moonweaver's Dawn, and GameWith's Valeriy team guide (updated Nov 5) adds the Overloaded team. Icy Veins' Valeriy pages could not be reached.

stats.circlet: ATK%
stats.goblet: ATK%
stats.sands: ATK% (Energy Recharge% if you need to cast his Burst every rotation)
stats.substats: ATK% > Energy Recharge > flat ATK > CRIT Rate (mainly with Favonius Sword). GenshinBuilds lists ATK% > flat ATK > Energy Recharge. Targets: 2,500 to 2,800+ Attack. Energy Recharge 150% or more, and 160 to 180% only if his Burst (60 Energy) is cast every rotation

talents.name: Elemental Skill: Offensive Defense: Fortress Advance
talents.why: Top priority in u7buy, since it makes his Attack-scaling shield. GenshinBuilds puts it second.

talents.name: Normal Attack
talents.why: Top priority in GenshinBuilds, because it boosts his Assault Command buffs and Charged Attack damage. u7buy puts it second.

talents.name: Elemental Burst: Firepower Focus: Thunderous Assault
talents.why: Lowest in both guides. It mainly adds personal damage.

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct (Mitya)
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds and strongest in u7buy. Mitya is the on-field Stellar-Conduct DPS, Odette enables the reaction, Valeriy shields Mitya and adds buffs, and Sucrose adds Elemental Mastery, crowd control and RES shred.

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct (Cyno)
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds. Cyno's Burst infuses his Normal Attacks with Electro, Mitya applies Electro off-field and Odette converts reactions. Valeriy boosts Electro Stellar-Conduct damage and shields.

teams.name: Cyno with Sucrose
teams.note: Odette enables Stellar-Conduct for Cyno, and Valeriy's long shield helps Cyno's longer rotations. Sucrose adds Elemental Mastery and Anemo support.

teams.name: Budget Mitya
teams.note: Cryo Traveler replaces Odette and keeps Stellar-Conduct active. His shield covers defense, so no dedicated healer is needed.

teams.name: Budget Mitya (Diona)
teams.note: A GameWith budget team of 4-star characters. Valeriy and Diona shield Mitya and keep Stellar-Conduct going.

teams.name: Overloaded (Clorinde)
teams.note: Rated 4 stars by GameWith. Valeriy's shield covers Clorinde's low interruption resistance and his Offensive Directive adds damage to her Electro hits. Durin and Chevreuse shred Pyro and Electro RES, and Chevreuse's passive only works if the whole party is Pyro or Electro. Best against large enemies and bosses.

weapons.name: Summit Shaper
weapons.why: Best in slot in both guides. It has the highest Attack (608 base) and a 49.6% Attack substat, plus Shield Strength, which makes his Attack-scaling shield much stronger. It has no Energy Recharge.

weapons.name: Finale of the Deep
weapons.why: The best 4-star for Attack (565 base, 27.6% Attack) and easy to obtain because you can craft it. No Energy Recharge, so use it when your team already gives him energy.

weapons.name: Favonius Sword
weapons.why: Best team utility. 61.3% Energy Recharge and Energy Particles help him cast his Burst (60 Energy) and the whole team. The lower Attack makes the shield a bit weaker.

weapons.name: Aquila Favonia
weapons.why: High base Attack, so it works as a strong Attack stat stick for his shield and buffs.

weapons.name: Fleuve Cendre Ferryman
weapons.why: Easy to obtain through fishing. 45.9% Energy Recharge and 510 base Attack make it a solid Energy Recharge option, though it makes no team particles.

weapons.name: Sapwood Blade
weapons.why: A balance of Attack (565 base) and Energy Recharge (30.6%). Its passive needs Dendro reactions, so it is a stat option in most teams.

weapons.name: Skyward Blade
weapons.why: An Energy Recharge option for teams where he needs to cast his Burst every rotation.

weapons.name: Calamity of Eshu
weapons.why: Attack option (565 base, 27.6% Attack). The passive is weak for a support, so it is mainly a stat stick.

weapons.name: Moonweaver's Dawn
weapons.why: Listed by GenshinBuilds for 7.2. 565 base Attack and a 27.6% Attack substat, the same stat line as Calamity of Eshu. Its passive boosts Burst Damage, which matters little because his Burst is the lowest talent priority, so it is mainly a stat stick.

weapons.name: Sacrificial Sword
weapons.why: Energy Recharge option (61.3%) with a chance to reset his Skill cooldown, so more shields. Lower base Attack.

weapons.name: Mistsplitter Reforged
weapons.why: CRIT DMG option. GenshinBuilds notes it is the most used weapon on its showcase data, but it is not built for a shield support.

weapons.name: Azurelight
weapons.why: CRIT Rate option from the same page. Only worth using if you already own it.

artifacts.name: Silken Moon's Serenade
artifacts.why: The primary choice. The 2-piece gives +20% Energy Recharge. The 4-piece gives a team-wide Elemental Mastery buff (+60, or +120 with a second Nod-Krai character) and +10% Lunar Reaction Damage for each distinct Gleaming Moon effect. It works off-field.

artifacts.name: Instructor
artifacts.why: The best alternative when another teammate already holds Silken Moon's Serenade. The 2-piece gives +80 Elemental Mastery. The 4-piece gives the party +120 Elemental Mastery for 8 seconds after a reaction. Trigger a reaction right before swapping to the on-field character.

artifacts.name: Noblesse Oblige
artifacts.why: For teams with Attack-scaling Damage dealers that do not use Elemental Mastery well. The 2-piece gives +20% Burst Damage and the 4-piece raises party Attack by 20% for 12 seconds. It does not stack.

artifacts.name: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
artifacts.why: Similar value to Noblesse Oblige, and better for teammates who benefit from an Elemental Damage bonus after a reaction than from Attack.

artifacts.name: Deepwood Memories
artifacts.why: For Lunar-Bloom or Dendro teams if no one else uses it. The 4-piece lowers Dendro RES by 30% for 8 seconds and can trigger off-field.

artifacts.name: Flower of Paradise Lost
artifacts.why: Only for Bloom, Hyperbloom or Burgeon teams, or when another teammate already holds Silken Moon's Serenade. The 2-piece gives +80 Elemental Mastery.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: Silken Moon's Serenade (Energy Recharge +20%) with Wanderer's Troupe (Elemental Mastery +80)
artifacts.why: A common community mix that covers her Energy Recharge and Elemental Mastery together. The Wanderer's Troupe effect is from my own knowledge.

info.role: Hydro Support (off-field Hydro and Moonsign enabler)

builds/aino.name: Aino
builds/aino.source: Several Aino build and team guides for version 7.1 (Icy Veins, KeqingMains, GenshinBuilds and Sportskeeda). They agree on Silken Moon's Serenade, Favonius Greatsword, a Burst-first talent order and Lunar-Charged as her best team type. They disagree on a few points: one guide puts the Skill first for talents while three put the Burst first, one guide wants Elemental Mastery on all three main stats while others favor Energy Recharge on Sands, and the Hu Tao Vaporize team is rated highly by one guide while another says Vaporize in AoE is unreliable. Her Moonsign passive is strongest with at least one other Nod-Krai character. The Wanderer's Troupe effect and the Rainslasher and Serpent Spine notes are from my own knowledge or only the community list.

stats.circlet: Elemental Mastery, CRIT Rate or CRIT Damage
stats.goblet: Elemental Mastery (Hydro Damage Bonus is a lower pick)
stats.sands: Energy Recharge or Elemental Mastery (Energy Recharge if you need to cast her Burst every rotation)
stats.substats: Energy Recharge first, until you reach her requirement. Then CRIT Rate, which helps trigger Favonius Greatsword. Then Elemental Mastery and CRIT Damage equally. Attack% last. Build more Elemental Mastery if she triggers Bloom, and Elemental Mastery plus CRIT if she deals Lunar-Charged Damage. Energy Recharge 155 to 205% with Favonius Greatsword (125 to 165% at C4), or 100 to 140% with Flame-Forged Insight. Targets: HP 16,500 to 19,000, Attack 1,050 to 1,200, CRIT Rate 60 to 75%, CRIT Damage 115 to 140%.

talents.name: Elemental Burst
talents.why: Her main contribution, since it applies Hydro off-field and its Damage scales with her Elemental Mastery.

talents.name: Elemental Skill
talents.why: Second. Her Skill and Normal Attack deal little Damage, so leaving them low costs little.

talents.name: Normal Attack
talents.why: Not worth leveling.

teams.name: Lunar-Charged: Flins, Ineffa, Sucrose
teams.note: Her strongest team type. Her off-field Hydro enables Lunar-Charged, and with Flins or Ineffa she reaches the higher Moonsign level that boosts Silken Moon's Serenade.

teams.name: Lunar-Charged: Ineffa, Ororon, Ifa
teams.note: Stronger Lunar-Charged Damage from Ifa and shorter rotations.

teams.name: Overvape: Ineffa, Yoimiya, Bennett
teams.note: Her Hydro with Lunar-Charged is just enough to enable Vaporize for a slow-applying Pyro Damage dealer. Ineffa is almost required.

teams.name: Overvape: Ineffa, Arlecchino, Bennett
teams.note: Aino adds Elemental Mastery from C1 and Silken Moon's Serenade for Arlecchino.

teams.name: Overvape: Ineffa, Chasca, Chevreuse
teams.note: Chevreuse's C6 gives Chasca a large Pyro and Electro Damage bonus. Aino is one of the few off-field Hydro appliers Chasca can use.

teams.name: Vaporize: Hu Tao, Furina, Citlali
teams.note: Rated highly by one guide. Citlali adds shields and RES shred. Another guide says Vaporize in AoE is less reliable.

teams.name: Vaporize: Yoimiya, Yelan, Ineffa
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds. Aino and Yelan supply off-field Hydro for Yoimiya's Vaporize, and Ineffa adds Electro support and Lunar-Charged.

teams.name: Hyperbloom: Nahida, Fischl, Kokomi
teams.note: She adds Dendro Core production and Silken Moon's Serenade uptime but cannot trigger Hyperbloom reliably alone.

teams.name: Lunar-Bloom: Lauma, Nilou, Baizhu
teams.note: Works if you want Lauma's Damage first. One guide says she is a poor fit unless Lauma has high Constellations.

teams.name: Freeze: Skirk, Dahlia, Escoffier
teams.note: Her AoE Hydro keeps enemies frozen. Escoffier shreds RES and fits the Cryo and Hydro core.

weapons.name: Favonius Greatsword
weapons.why: The best general pick. It has 61.3% Energy Recharge, and CRIT hits make Energy Particles that cover most of her Energy needs and help her team. She needs a few CRIT Rate substats to trigger it reliably. The stat targets assume this weapon.

weapons.name: Flame-Forged Insight
weapons.why: One of the best for her reaction Damage: large Elemental Mastery and flat Energy after Lunar-Charged, Bloom and similar reactions, even off-field. It was an event weapon and can no longer be obtained if you missed it.

weapons.name: Master Key
weapons.why: Craftable in Nod-Krai, so it is easy to obtain. It gives 61.3% Energy Recharge and Elemental Mastery on any reaction. A near-identical alternative with a bit less Elemental Mastery.

weapons.name: Forest Regalia
weapons.why: A strong pick for Lunar-Bloom teams. It leaves a Leaf after certain Dendro and Hydro reactions that gives a teammate Elemental Mastery. The Leaf can be hard to pick up.

weapons.name: Makhaira Aquamarine
weapons.why: Gives Elemental Mastery and a team-wide Attack buff based on her Elemental Mastery. Best in teams that are not Energy-hungry.

weapons.name: Katsuragikiri Nagamasa
weapons.why: Helps meet her Energy Recharge target with its Energy Recharge substat and flat Energy refund. Good if you already own it refined.

weapons.name: Sacrificial Greatsword
weapons.why: Less flexible than Favonius Greatsword, but it can battery a Hydro teammate when highly refined.

weapons.name: Rainslasher
weapons.why: A common community pick for her. It is easy to obtain, but it adds little for her support role.

weapons.name: Serpent Spine
weapons.why: Boosts her personal Damage, but it is better kept for a Claymore main DPS.

weapons.name: Wolf's Gravestone
weapons.why: Not worth using. Its party Attack buff has poor uptime and is unreliable for her.

artifacts.name: Noblesse Oblige
artifacts.why: Preferred set. Using Mika's Burst raises the whole team's ATK by 20%, which benefits the Physical DPS he supports. If another character already uses Noblesse, don't double up the buff.

artifacts.name: Ocean-Hued Clam
artifacts.why: The next best choice, although it is less ideal than Noblesse. Use it when another party member already runs Noblesse Oblige. (General knowledge: its bonus is based on his healing, so it fits his kit.)

builds/mika.name: Mika
builds/mika.source: Icy Veins Mika build guide (weapons, artifacts, stats, ER targets, teams). Reasons marked as general knowledge are my own explanation, not quoted from a guide.

stats.circlet: Healing Bonus (or CRIT Rate). Healing Bonus gives a greater benefit than an HP% circlet.
stats.goblet: HP%
stats.sands: Energy Recharge or HP% (ER if you need it for Burst uptime)
stats.substats: Energy Recharge (to target) > CRIT Rate (if using Favonius Lance) > HP% > HP. ER target: about 200-220% at C1-C3, about 160-180% at C4+.

talents.name: Elemental Skill: Starfrost Swirl
talents.why: Level it first. The attack speed buff Mika gives your DPS scales with this talent, and Icy Veins calls it incredibly important. The jump from 9 to 10 is expensive, so 9 is a fine stopping point on a budget.

talents.name: Elemental Burst: Skyfeather Song
talents.why: Level it second. It is the team-wide heal and the healing scales with his max HP. Pocket Tactics suggests levelling it alongside the Skill.

talents.name: Normal Attack
talents.why: Skip it. Mika is a support and his value comes from the Skill and Burst, so Normal Attack levels are not worth the materials.

teams.name: Physical team 1
teams.note: Eula is the main DPS and Raiden is the sub DPS. Furina and Mika support.

teams.name: Physical team 2
teams.note: Eula is the main DPS and Ineffa is the sub DPS. Furina and Mika support.

teams.name: Physical team 3
teams.note: Freminet is the main DPS. Fischl and Xingqiu are sub DPS.

teams.name: Freeze team 1
teams.note: Skirk is the main DPS. Yelan and Furina are sub DPS.

teams.name: Freeze team 2
teams.note: Wriothesley is the main DPS. Yelan and Furina are sub DPS.

teams.name: Wanderer team
teams.note: Wanderer is the main DPS. Faruzan, Mika and Bennett support.

weapons.name: Symphonist of Scents
weapons.why: Best in slot per Icy Veins. It gives massive bonuses that Mika can use well because he heals the team. The catch is that it makes his Energy Recharge requirements harder to reach, so you need to build ER on your artifacts to make up for it.

weapons.name: Dialogues of the Desert Sages
weapons.why: Less supportive than Symphonist, but it scales off HP%, which is still an important stat for Mika's healing and Soulwind buff. A good pick if you own it and have enough Energy Recharge from artifacts.

weapons.name: Favonius Lance
weapons.why: The best option for Energy Recharge. It also lowers the team's Energy Recharge requirements by generating particles. It gives Mika some CRIT Rate too, so that stat gets useful substats if you use it.

weapons.name: Prototype Starglitter
weapons.why: A free (craftable) alternative listed by Icy Veins. Good for a player without a 5-star or Favonius Lance.

weapons.name: The Catch
weapons.why: A free fishing weapon listed by Icy Veins as an alternative. It gives high Energy Recharge, which helps Mika use his Burst more often.

artifacts.name: Scarlet Proof
artifacts.why: Best in slot in both guides. The 2-piece gives +18% Attack. The 4-piece gives +16% CRIT Rate and +40% Stellar-Swirl Damage for 10 seconds after a Stellar Swirl.

artifacts.name: Viridescent Venerer
artifacts.why: The alternative, usually 1-2% behind Scarlet Proof. The 2-piece gives +15% Anemo Damage. The 4-piece raises Swirl and Stellar-Swirl Damage and shreds Cryo RES by 40%. Useful when no one else shreds RES.

artifacts.name: Resolution of Sojourner
artifacts.why: The most-used set in the community on GenshinBuilds. The page does not say why.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: Gladiator's Finale (Attack +18%) with A Day Carved From Rising Winds (Attack +18%)
artifacts.why: GenshinBuilds' temporary Attack mix while you farm Scarlet Proof. 4-star versions of these pieces also work. The set effects are from my own knowledge.

builds/vesna.name: Vesna
builds/vesna.source: Icy Veins Vesna build guide (S+, updated Sep 2026) and team guide, and GenshinBuilds Vesna page (v7.1). Icy Veins states star ratings only for Whitelake Frostfeather (5-star), New Bough (4-star) and Silver Light (4-star); the other star ratings are from my own knowledge, and Emberwell and Heretic's Molten Blade are assumed 4-star from their base Attack. Exaiphanes Blade is not in Icy Veins' list for her and appears only on GenshinBuilds' community list. GenshinBuilds' substat order conflicts with its own team cards, so I used Icy Veins' order. The 2pc set names and their effects come from GenshinBuilds' farming note and my own knowledge. Harbinger of Dawn comes from GenshinBuilds' community list.

stats.circlet: CRIT Rate or CRIT Damage
stats.goblet: Attack% or Elemental Mastery (GenshinBuilds says Attack% beats Anemo Damage)
stats.sands: Attack% or Elemental Mastery (two Attack% main stats are slightly better)
stats.substats: CRIT Rate > CRIT Damage > Attack% > Elemental Mastery > Energy Recharge. Targets with her best weapon and decently built artifacts: Attack 2,600+, Elemental Mastery 100+, Energy Recharge 100-130%, CRIT Rate 69-84%, CRIT Damage 180%+. With a second Anemo character she needs 120-140% Energy Recharge per rotation, and 150-170% without one.

talents.name: Elemental Skill: The Art of Victory
talents.why: Top priority in both guides, and her largest damage source. The guides give the order only, not target levels.

talents.name: Elemental Burst: For the Tsaritsa!
talents.why: Second priority.

talents.name: Normal Attack: Vila Blade Dance
talents.why: Icy Veins says not to level it, since it only applies Anemo and cannot deal direct Stellar-Swirl damage.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Vodyanitsa, Cryo Traveler, Odette (SS)
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds and the team Icy Veins uses for its rotation. Vodyanitsa lowers Anemo RES, buffs Stellar-Swirl Damage and heals. Cryo Traveler is a free character.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Odette, Vodyanitsa, Qiqi (S+)
teams.note: Rated S+ by GenshinBuilds. Qiqi provides constant Cryo application.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Vodyanitsa, Faruzan, Odette
teams.note: Icy Veins' first listed team. It has no healer or shielder, so it is harder to play. Odette can give up to 60% Stellar Damage.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Cryo Traveler, Faruzan, Odette
teams.note: Faruzan adds a damage buff and Anemo RES shred, especially at C6. The team has no sustain.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Cryo Traveler, Faruzan, Diona
teams.note: Diona is a decent 4-star option, with more buffs at C6.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Vodyanitsa, Faruzan, Escoffier
teams.note: Escoffier applies Cryo steadily and deals some off-field damage.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Qiqi, Sucrose, Diona
teams.note: Sucrose adds a lot of Elemental Mastery, which matters for Stellar-Swirl damage.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Lan Yan, Cryo Traveler, Qiqi
teams.note: Lan Yan can carry Thrilling Tales of Dragon Slayers and gives a shield.

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Venti, Nicole, Odette
teams.note: Nicole gives a large party-wide Attack buff. Venti adds no large Stellar-Swirl buffs.

weapons.name: Beyond the Chrysalis
weapons.why: Her signature weapon and best in slot in both guides. It cycles CRIT Damage, Stellar-Swirl Damage and Energy after each Skill or Burst. The CRIT Damage substat suits any sword user.

weapons.name: Whitelake Frostfeather
weapons.why: Second in both guides. It stacks Attack after Skill hits, and at 3 stacks boosts Stellar Glimmer CRIT Damage and restores Energy. A decent 5-star alternative (Icy Veins).

weapons.name: Azurelight
weapons.why: A solid stat stick with CRIT Rate. It gives Attack after her Skill, and extra Attack and CRIT Damage at 0 Energy.

weapons.name: Light of Foliar Incision
weapons.why: Fourth in Icy Veins' team damage ranking, ahead of several other 5-stars.

weapons.name: Absolution
weapons.why: CRIT Damage substat and a stacking Damage bonus. Ranked at the same level as Light of Foliar Incision.

weapons.name: Exaiphanes Blade
weapons.why: The Traveler's free signature sword from the Snezhnaya archon quest. GenshinBuilds lists it among the community's most-used weapons for her, with a CRIT Rate substat. Icy Veins does not list it for her.

weapons.name: Uraku Misugiri
weapons.why: A CRIT Damage option that ranks around 110% in the guide's team ranking.

weapons.name: Primordial Jade Cutter
weapons.why: Adds 44% CRIT Rate, which can overcap her CRIT Rate in Cryo teams, so it ranks lower.

weapons.name: Emberwell
weapons.why: The best free-to-play weapon, craftable in Snezhnaya. It has an Elemental Mastery substat, grants Attack after reactions and boosts Stellar Glimmer Damage, even off-field.

weapons.name: New Bough
weapons.why: A gacha 4-star and the guide's third pick (R5). It has a CRIT Damage substat and gives Attack and Elemental Mastery after her Skill. A consolation prize if you miss her signature.

weapons.name: Silver Light
weapons.why: An event-exclusive 4-star with an Attack percent substat. It gives Elemental Mastery after each Skill use, up to 2 stacks.

weapons.name: Heretic's Molten Blade
weapons.why: A Battle Pass option with a CRIT Rate substat. Its Attack ramps after her Skill (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: Wolf-Fang
weapons.why: CRIT Rate substat and Skill and Burst Damage. Ranked at about 100% in Icy Veins' list.

weapons.name: Finale of the Deep
weapons.why: A free-to-play pick, ranked with a healer in the team.

weapons.name: Iron Sting
weapons.why: A craftable Elemental Mastery option at the bottom of Icy Veins' ranking.

weapons.name: Harbinger of Dawn
weapons.why: A free CRIT Damage option from GenshinBuilds' community list. A 3-star weapon you can wish for on any banner or earn from story quests.

artifacts.name: Night of the Sky's Unveiling
artifacts.why: His best set in both guides. The 2-piece gives +80 Elemental Mastery. The 4-piece raises the party's Moonsign level, which unlocks a CRIT Rate boost and Lunar Reaction Damage buffs. It works best with a second Nod-Krai / Moonsign character in the party.

artifacts.name: Thundering Fury
artifacts.why: Icy Veins' second-best set. The 2-piece adds 15% Electro Damage and the 4-piece adds 20% Lunar-Charged Damage, a viable choice for Lunar-Charged characters.

artifacts.name: Gilded Dreams
artifacts.why: A general fallback listed by GenshinBuilds.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: Gladiator's Finale (Attack +18%), Gilded Dreams (EM +80) or Emblem of Severed Fate (ER +20%)
artifacts.why: Flexible 2-piece options from GenshinBuilds. Attack +18%: Gladiator's Finale, Resolution of Sojourner or Shimenawa's Reminiscence. Elemental Mastery +80: Gilded Dreams, Instructor, Wanderer's Troupe or Flower of Paradise Lost. Energy Recharge +20%: Emblem of Severed Fate, Silken Moon's Serenade, Scholar or The Exile. It suggests the Attack +18% set only if many of his hits are unbuffed Normal Attacks.

builds/flins.name: Flins
builds/flins.source: Icy Veins Flins build and team guides, and GenshinBuilds Flins page (v7.1). Icy Veins lists teams without ranking or roles. The guides disagree on the substat order; both are noted. Star ratings were mostly not stated by the sources; the ones given are from my own knowledge.

stats.circlet: CRIT Rate or CRIT Damage
stats.goblet: Attack% or Elemental Mastery (Icy Veins warns against an Electro Damage goblet, since Lunar damage does not scale from Damage% bonuses)
stats.sands: Attack% or Elemental Mastery
stats.substats: CRIT Rate / CRIT Damage > Attack% and Elemental Mastery > Energy Recharge (Icy Veins; GenshinBuilds lists Energy Recharge first). ER target: about 120-130%, lower with an ER weapon. Icy Veins' targets with Prospector's Shovel: HP 18,000-20,000, Attack about 2,000, CRIT Rate 45-55%, CRIT Damage 170-200%, ER 120-140%.

talents.name: Elemental Burst: Ancient Ritual: Cometh the Night
talents.why: Top priority in both guides. His Mini Burst costs 30 Energy and the standard Burst costs 80. The guides give the order only, not target levels.

talents.name: Elemental Skill: Ancient Rite: Arcane Light
talents.why: Second priority. The levels are my reading of the order, not from the guides.

talents.name: Normal Attack
talents.why: Both guides say Normal Attacks can mostly be ignored.

teams.name: Lunar-Charged: Columbina, Ineffa, Sucrose
teams.note: First on Icy Veins' best-teams list. Ineffa is his best teammate: a shield, off-field Electro and Elemental Mastery. Columbina is his strongest Hydro option and can hold Thrilling Tales of Dragon Slayers for an Attack buff.

teams.name: Free-to-play: Aino, Fischl, Sucrose
teams.note: A free-to-play-friendly team from Icy Veins.

teams.name: Free-to-play: Xingqiu, Jahoda, Aino
teams.note: A free-to-play-friendly team from Icy Veins.

teams.note: A free-to-play-friendly team from Icy Veins.

teams.note: A free-to-play-friendly team from Icy Veins. Avoid generic buffers like Furina: Icy Veins says they are very bad for Flins, since his damage scales only from Attack and Elemental Mastery.

weapons.name: Bloodsoaked Ruins
weapons.why: His signature weapon and best in slot in both guides. It adds Lunar-Charged Damage and CRIT Damage buffs, restores Energy, and generates Energy particles, which significantly reduces his Energy requirements.

weapons.name: Staff of the Scarlet Sands
weapons.why: Gives high CRIT Rate and converts Elemental Mastery into Attack, which suits how Flins scales.

weapons.name: Fractured Halo
weapons.why: A solid 5-star option with strong base stats and an Attack boost after his Skill or Burst. GenshinBuilds notes its damage buff applies while he is on the field.

weapons.name: Staff of Homa
weapons.why: A strong general-purpose weapon. It adds HP and CRIT Damage and converts HP into Attack.

weapons.name: Primordial Jade Winged-Spear
weapons.why: High base Attack and CRIT Rate with stacking bonuses. Icy Veins calls it a dependable choice.

weapons.name: Deathmatch
weapons.why: One of his best 4-star options. It has a CRIT Rate main stat and an Attack boost that is easily met in single-target fights.

weapons.name: Tamayuratei no Ohanashi
weapons.why: An event weapon that Icy Veins calls the best free-to-play option for Flins. It gives Energy Recharge and an Attack boost after using his Skill.

weapons.name: Prospector's Shovel
weapons.why: A craftable weapon that boosts Electro-Charged and Lunar-Charged Damage. The build guide's stat targets assume it, and it is also called his best free-to-play weapon in one place.

weapons.name: Symphonist of Scents
weapons.why: Ranked 5th by GenshinBuilds, with a CRIT Damage substat. Its passive grants Attack and Elemental Mastery when allies trigger reactions.

weapons.name: Lumidouce Elegy
weapons.why: Its passive raises Attack and can restore Energy. A viable 5-star option per Icy Veins, with buffs that scale with Elemental Mastery.

weapons.name: Engulfing Lightning
weapons.why: Converts Energy Recharge into Attack and suits burst-focused play.

weapons.name: Skyward Spine
weapons.why: A fallback for players without other 5-stars, giving Energy Recharge and extra damage. GenshinBuilds says to use it when burst uptime is the bottleneck, at some cost to damage.

weapons.name: Missive Windspear
weapons.why: A free polearm that gains Attack and Elemental Mastery after reactions. A solid alternative if you already own it.

weapons.name: Kitain Cross Spear
weapons.why: A craftable fallback that adds Elemental Mastery and Energy utility.

weapons.name: Ballad of the Fjords
weapons.why: A free event polearm that gives CRIT Rate and Elemental Mastery. Listed by GenshinBuilds as a budget alternative.

artifacts.name: Night of the Sky's Unveiling
artifacts.why: Best in slot in both guides. The 2-piece gives +80 Elemental Mastery. The 4-piece gives her up to +30% CRIT Rate after party members trigger Lunar reactions, and boosts party Lunar Reaction Damage.

artifacts.name: Resolution of Sojourner
artifacts.why: Listed in the community's most-used builds on GenshinBuilds. The page does not say why.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: Night of the Sky's Unveiling (Elemental Mastery +80) with Wanderer's Troupe (Elemental Mastery +80)
artifacts.why: One of GenshinBuilds' community mixes. Another is Gilded Dreams with Wanderer's Troupe or Night of the Sky's Unveiling. The set effects here are from my own knowledge.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: Gilded Dreams (Elemental Mastery +80) with Wanderer's Troupe (Elemental Mastery +80)
artifacts.why: Also on GenshinBuilds' community list. The set effects here are from my own knowledge.

Nocturne's Curtain Call, Surf's Up and Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds appear only on GenshinBuilds. stats.goblet: Elemental Mastery

stats.substats: CRIT Rate / CRIT Damage > Elemental Mastery > Energy Recharge. weapons.name: Reliquary of Truth
weapons.why: Her signature weapon and first in both guides. It has a 88.2% CRIT Damage substat, gives Elemental Mastery from her Skill, and boosts CRIT Damage after Lunar-Bloom damage.

weapons.name: Nightweaver's Looking Glass
weapons.why: Second on Icy Veins. High Elemental Mastery, and its passive boosts Bloom and Lunar-Bloom damage after her Skill. It works off-field and suits quickswap teams that recast her Skill.

weapons.name: Nocturne's Curtain Call
weapons.why: Second on GenshinBuilds: a CRIT Damage weapon that restores Energy after her Burst. A reliable pick for burst-focused teams.

weapons.name: Starcaller's Watch
weapons.why: A big Elemental Mastery boost and a damage bonus after a shield is created. Strong in reaction-heavy teams.

weapons.name: Sunny Morning Sleep-In
weapons.why: A smoother option with a lower ceiling. It gives large Elemental Mastery after Skill and Burst hits and restores Energy.

weapons.name: Tome of the Eternal Flow
weapons.why: CRIT Damage substat and an HP-based Charged Attack bonus. GenshinBuilds says it is only worthwhile if her kit uses that scaling.

weapons.name: A Thousand Floating Dreams
weapons.why: Gives her Elemental Mastery and an Elemental Damage bonus, and shares Elemental Mastery with the party.

weapons.name: Surf's Up
weapons.why: A CRIT Damage weapon that suits rotations using Normal Attacks to stack Seeds (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: Kagura's Verity
weapons.why: Big base Attack, CRIT Damage substat, and stacking Skill damage. Ranked in Icy Veins' list.

weapons.name: Blackmarrow Lantern
weapons.why: Icy Veins' best free-to-play weapon, and the one its stat targets assume. It boosts Bloom and Lunar-Bloom damage.

weapons.name: Dawning Frost
weapons.why: CRIT Damage substat, and her Charged Attacks and Skill give Elemental Mastery. Icy Veins ranks it third (R5).

weapons.name: The Widsith
weapons.why: A high-ceiling budget choice. On field entry it gives a random strong buff: Attack, Elemental Damage or Elemental Mastery.

weapons.name: Sacrificial Jade
weapons.why: CRIT Rate substat and an off-field boost to Health and Elemental Mastery. Listed by Icy Veins as a lower pick.

weapons.name: Solar Pearl
weapons.why: CRIT Rate substat and a stacking Skill and Burst damage bonus.

weapons.name: Mappa Mare
weapons.why: Elemental Mastery substat and an Elemental Damage bonus after reactions. The lowest-rated pick on Icy Veins' list.

artifacts.name: Silken Moon's Serenade
artifacts.why: GenshinBuilds' top pick. It gives a team-wide EM boost (requires Ascendant Gleam), and Icy Veins says to include it in most Ascendant Gleam teams. Its 2-piece gives 20% Energy Recharge.

artifacts.name: Aubade of Morningstar and Moon
artifacts.why: Best for maximizing her off-field personal damage through a Lunar Reaction bonus. It does not work on-field and is only worth using if your team has Ascendant Gleam.

artifacts.name: Night of the Sky's Unveiling
artifacts.why: Use this for on-field Columbina. Its 4-piece boosts CRIT Rate and Lunar Reaction DMG.

artifacts.name: Deepwood Memories
artifacts.why: Its 4-piece shreds 30% Dendro RES, a large damage boost for Lunar-Bloom teams. Use it if no other support can.

artifacts.name: Tenacity of the Millelith
artifacts.why: Its 2-piece gives 20% HP and its 4-piece gives nearby party members 20% ATK and 30% Shield Strength. Good in attack-scaling teams, such as with Flins or Ineffa.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: Tenacity of the Millelith (HP +20%), Gilded Dreams (EM +80) or Silken Moon's Serenade (ER +20%)
artifacts.why: The flexible 2-piece options listed by GenshinBuilds. Max HP +20%: Tenacity of the Millelith or Vourukasha's Glow. Elemental Mastery +80: Gilded Dreams, Instructor or Flower of Paradise Lost. Energy Recharge +20%: Silken Moon's Serenade, Emblem of Severed Fate, Scholar or The Exile.

builds/xiao.name: Xiao
builds/xiao.source: Icy Veins Xiao build guide (updated for 7.0, B-tier) and team guide (last updated Apr 5, 2026), and Pocket Tactics Xiao build (published Mar 2025, shows 4.4 art). They differ on the best set: Icy Veins ranks Long Night's Oath first, Pocket Tactics ranks Vermillion Hereafter first (older guide). Icy Veins' team guide lists no complete teams, so most teams come from Pocket Tactics, and the Double Anemo/Pyro, Xianyun-Faruzan-Zhongli and Triple Anemo lineups are my own assembly from Icy Veins' support notes. Pocket Tactics gives lower CRIT Damage targets (140%). The star ratings of Prospector's Drill, Favonius Lance, Missive Windspear, Wavebreaker's Fin, Prototype Starglitter and White Tassel are from my own knowledge, since Icy Veins does not state them. The effects of Vortex Vanquisher, Calamity Queller, Blackcliff Pole, Skyward Spine and Staff of the Scarlet Sands are also from my own knowledge.

stats.circlet: CRIT Damage or CRIT Rate (about a 1:2 ratio of CRIT Rate to CRIT Damage). Avoid Energy Recharge as a main stat.
stats.goblet: Anemo Damage Bonus (Attack% only if it has strong CRIT substats)
stats.sands: Attack%
stats.substats: Icy Veins: Energy Recharge > CRIT Rate = CRIT Damage > Attack%. Pocket Tactics: CRIT Rate, CRIT Damage, Attack%, then Energy Recharge. Targets (Icy Veins, with a decently built set and his best weapon): HP 18,000 to 20,000, Attack 2,100 to 2,300, CRIT Rate 70% to 75%, CRIT Damage 190% to 220%, Energy Recharge 120% to 140% (less with an Anemo battery), Anemo Damage Bonus 46.6%.

stats.circlet: CRIT Rate or CRIT Damage (Icy Veins prefers it over Attack%, which is fine until you find a good CRIT circlet)
stats.goblet: Cryo Damage Bonus or Attack% (Icy Veins: roughly equal with Golden Troupe, and Attack% is better for healing)
stats.sands: Attack% or Energy Recharge (Energy Recharge only if needed to reach her Energy Recharge target)
stats.substats: Icy Veins: Energy Recharge > CRIT Rate / CRIT Damage > Attack%. GenshinBuilds: Energy Recharge > CRIT Rate > CRIT Damage > Attack%. Icy Veins' targets with Deathmatch and Golden Troupe (with Skirk, Furina and Mona): HP 19,000-21,000, Attack 1,650-1,800, CRIT Rate 75-85%, CRIT Damage 165-190%, Energy Recharge 180-200%. Energy Recharge needs drop with three Cryo units or more particle generation. GenshinBuilds gives no target, only a 200%+ figure under Engulfing Lightning.

talents.why: Top priority in both guides. The guides give the order only, not target levels.

talents.name: Elemental Burst: Scoring Cuts
talents.why: Second priority. Icy Veins does not name it, so the page's mapping is inferred, and the levels are my reading of the order.

talents.name: Normal Attack: Kitchen Skills
talents.why: Both guides say it can be ignored.

teams.name: Permafrost Freeze: Citlali (S)
teams.note: Rated S by GenshinBuilds, with Citlali as a second Cryo support.

teams.name: Freeze: Skirk, Furina, Mona

teams.name: Freeze: Ganyu, Furina, Shenhe
teams.note: Shenhe's buff is especially useful for swap-heavy Cryo DPS like Ganyu.

teams.name: Freeze: Neuvillette, Furina, Citlali
teams.note: Citlali's 20% Hydro RES Shred suits Neuvillette. Neuvillette gets only one Draconic Stack here.

teams.name: Freeze: Ayato, Furina, Yelan
teams.note: Yelan is a Hydro sub-DPS option that needs less Energy Recharge.

teams.name: Freeze: Kokomi, Furina, Yelan
teams.note: Kokomi provides her own healing, so Escoffier does not need her Burst.

teams.name: Freeze: Kaeya, Furina, Chongyun

teams.name: Freeze: Sandrone, Qiqi, Yae Miko

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct: Cryo Traveler, Odette, Yae Miko
teams.note: The Traveler's 15-second cooldowns fit Escoffier's rotation.

teams.name: Pyro Melt: Arlecchino, Bennett, Citlali

teams.name: Pyro Melt: Yoimiya, Bennett, Citlali
teams.note: The same Cryo core with a Pyro DPS.

teams.name: Pyro Melt: Gaming, Bennett, Citlali
teams.note: The same Cryo core with a Pyro DPS.

weapons.name: Symphonist of Scents
weapons.why: Her signature weapon and first in both guides. It gives Attack to the active character and boosts her healing. GenshinBuilds says it gives the highest raw damage if her sands cover the Burst's Energy cost.

weapons.name: Engulfing Lightning
weapons.why: Second in both guides. It gives a 55.1% Energy Recharge substat and converts excess Energy Recharge into Attack. Strong when she needs high Energy Recharge, but weak in triple-Cryo teams (Icy Veins).

weapons.name: Calamity Queller
weapons.why: Large Attack and an elemental Damage bonus that ramps after her Skill and Burst. Icy Veins says it is good for both damage and healing.

weapons.name: Fractured Halo
weapons.why: A solid stat stick with CRIT Damage and Attack percent, plus an off-field damage passive (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: Staff of Homa
weapons.why: A damage-ceiling pick with CRIT Damage and no Energy Recharge, so the team must supply Energy. Icy Veins calls it identical to Fractured Halo.

weapons.name: Sacrificer's Staff
weapons.why: Icy Veins' best 4-star option, with CRIT Rate, Attack percent and Energy Recharge. It can be her second-best weapon when refined. GenshinBuilds calls it a budget Energy Recharge option with a Skill-reset passive.

weapons.name: Deathmatch
weapons.why: An accessible 4-star from the Battle Pass, but its CRIT Rate can overcap (Icy Veins). GenshinBuilds says it is strong on groups and flat in single-target fights.

weapons.name: Kitain Cross Spear
weapons.why: A craftable Energy fix that refunds Energy after her Skill (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: Skyward Spine
weapons.why: A fallback with 36.8% Energy Recharge and a CRIT Rate passive (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: Lumidouce Elegy
weapons.why: Steady off-field damage, though its Burning clause rarely triggers outside Dendro teams (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: Vortex Vanquisher
weapons.why: Reliable Attack percent, but it adds no Energy Recharge (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: Favonius Lance
weapons.why: Weak for her own damage. Useful only for Energy particles (Icy Veins), or as a team-play choice that generates particles on CRIT hits (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: Tamayuratei no Ohanashi
weapons.why: A free-to-play option and a 4-star filler when no Energy Recharge polearm is available. Icy Veins notes it is no longer obtainable.

artifacts.name: Tenacity of the Millelith
artifacts.why: The default set for almost every team. The 4-piece gives the whole team a 20% ATK buff, which suits her ATK-scaling teammates, and the 2-piece gives her 20% HP to raise her healing and quill buffs. Use it unless another character already wears it.

artifacts.name: Song of Days Past
artifacts.why: A supportive alternative when you already have 65,000 HP, which can happen with her signature weapon or a high-HP setup. It is recommended less than Tenacity of the Millelith, which also gives her HP. Icy Veins also suggests it for Freeze teams such as Skirk or Lohen, especially when another character already wears Tenacity of the Millelith.

artifacts.name: Instructor
artifacts.why: A beginner-friendly fallback listed by Icy Veins. The 4-piece gives the whole party Elemental Mastery after a reaction. It is a 4-star set that costs a lot of HP, so her HP target is harder to reach.

artifacts.name: Scroll set (named "Scroll" in the video; likely Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City)
artifacts.why: Another supportive option, only if your team can use the damage bonus and you are already near the HP cap. Check the exact set name in the video, because the captions only say "Scroll".

artifacts.name: Tenacity of the Millelith + Vourukasha's Glow (2pc + 2pc, HP +20% each)
artifacts.why: Use this when Tenacity of the Millelith is already worn elsewhere, for example by Furina in a freeze team. It gives her extra HP until the 65,000 HP cap, where her quills stop growing.

builds/vodinita.name: Vodyanitsa
builds/vodinita.source: Zy0x guide transcript (other character names as spelled in the auto-captions) Re-checked 2026-10-17 against Icy Veins (Vodyanitsa build and team guides, updated for 7.1) and GenshinBuilds (v7.1).

stats.circlet: HP%
stats.goblet: HP%
stats.sands: HP%
stats.substats: HP% > HP > Energy Recharge (only if you use her Burst regularly)

teams.name: Skirk freeze (her best, new premium team)
teams.note: The fourth slot Skirk was missing. If you lack Escoffier or Furina, use the best hydro or cryo options you have.

teams.name: Vesna stellar swirl
teams.note: A comfortable upgrade over other healers such as Qiqi or Diona. The last slot is flexible, for example Faruzan. Without Odette use a generic cryo like Qiqi or C6 Diona.

teams.name: Mizuki stellar swirl
teams.note: Vodyanitsa takes the slot of a C6 Faruzan. It needs enough cryo application, so time your Cryo Traveler skill right before swapping to Mizuki.

teams.name: Hydro Varka (name as captioned)
teams.note: An alternative to Varka's pyro teams. Mona can replace Furina, and Sucrose can replace Venti.

teams.name: Lohen freeze
teams.note: A shorter rotation with good buff uptime. Another hexerei unit such as Prune, or another hydro, can replace a slot.

teams.name: Neuvillette freeze
teams.note: An upgrade on his existing freeze team, and even better with his C1.

teams.name: Sandrone stellar conduct
teams.note: She works as a flexible last slot with cryo resistance reduction, healing and interruption resistance. GenshinBuilds lists Yae Miko and Odette as the other two slots.

teams.name: Wriothesley freeze
teams.note: A Cryo-focused freeze team similar to Lohen's, listed by Icy Veins.

teams.name: Ayato freeze
teams.note: A Hydro-focused freeze team. Vodyanitsa adds Hydro RES shred, healing and Hydro DMG buffs for Ayato. Listed by Icy Veins.

weapons.name: Hymn of the Maelstrom
weapons.why: Gives about 66% HP from the stat line plus up to 21% more HP, a 4% healing bonus and up to 42% ATK for the on-field character, scaling with her HP up to 60,000. The buff has full uptime and also helps sub-DPS characters, but in practice it is only about 5-7% more team damage than Thrilling Tales. Use it if you have it; the video does not recommend pulling for it and ranks her C1 and C2 above it.

weapons.name: Any HP-scaling 5★ catalyst
weapons.why: Only worth it in teams without an attack-scaling carry, such as a Neuvillette team, where the extra HP matters more than an ATK buff. No specific weapon is named in the video. With an attack scaler in the team, Thrilling Tales is better.

weapons.name: Jadefall's Splendor
weapons.why: An HP-scaling option listed by Icy Veins. After her Burst or a shield it restores Energy and grants Elemental DMG Bonus based on her Max HP, up to 44% at R5. It helps her reach her HP target and adds some utility.

weapons.name: Everlasting Moonglow
weapons.why: A solid HP-scaling weapon listed by Icy Veins. It raises her Healing Bonus and adds Normal Attack damage based on her Max HP. It also restores Energy from Normal Attacks for 12 seconds after her Burst.

weapons.name: Sacrificial Jade
weapons.why: A generic HP stat stick that works for teams without an attack scaler. It gives only slightly more HP than Thrilling Tales, so it loses whenever you have an attack-scaling main DPS.

weapons.name: Prototype Amber
weapons.why: Another HP catalyst that is fine as a stat stick, but it gives little more HP than Thrilling Tales. Pick it only when your team has no attack scaler to buff.

weapons.name: Waveriding Whirl
weapons.why: A fine HP catalyst for teams without an attack scaler, in the same group as Sacrificial Jade and Prototype Amber. Thrilling Tales is better if your carry scales with ATK.

weapons.name: Ash-Graven Drinking Horn
weapons.why: Icy Veins and GenshinBuilds both list it as a free HP-scaling option. It has 510 base ATK and 41.3% HP, the same stat line as Prototype Amber, and its passive deals AoE damage equal to 40-80% of her Max HP once every 15 seconds. Use it as a stat stick in teams without an attack scaler; Thrilling Tales is still better when your carry scales with ATK.

weapons.name: Thrilling Tales of Dragon Slayers
weapons.why: The standard best choice for nearly all her teams, and it is free to get. At R5 it gives the next character you swap into 48% ATK for 10 seconds (once every 20 seconds) and 35% HP from the stat line for her. Use her skill, then swap straight to your main DPS. Uptime is about 50% in rotations shorter than 20 seconds, but in long ones like Skirk it buffs every rotation.

artifacts.name: Gilded Dreams
artifacts.why: Best set for her Reverse Melt build in GenshinBuilds and Game8. Off-element teammates give Elemental Mastery and same-element teammates give Attack, once every 8 seconds after an Elemental Reaction. Game8 lists 80 Elemental Mastery from the 2-piece and up to 14% Attack per same-element teammate and 50 Elemental Mastery per different-element teammate from the 4-piece, each capped at 3 characters.

artifacts.name: Emblem of Severed Fate
artifacts.why: Her Burst scales with Energy Recharge, so this set adds Burst damage equal to 25% of Energy Recharge, up to 75%. GenshinBuilds says it can beat Gilded Dreams at 130% Energy Recharge or more, and Game8 recommends it for non-Freeze teams.

artifacts.name: Blizzard Strayer
artifacts.why: First pick for Freeze teams. The 2-piece gives +15% Cryo Damage, and the 4-piece gives +20% CRIT Rate against Cryo-affected enemies and another +20% against Frozen enemies. It is also the most used set in showcased builds (68%).

artifacts.name: Noblesse Oblige
artifacts.why: Her Burst gives the party +20% Attack for 12 seconds, and it does not stack with another Noblesse Oblige. Use it when no teammate runs it. The 2-piece gives +20% Burst Damage. It is second in Game8's Sub DPS list and used in 63% of showcased builds.

artifacts.name: Blizzard Strayer (2-piece) + Noblesse Oblige (2-piece)
artifacts.why: GenshinBuilds' pick for her in the Hu Tao and Eula teams. You keep the Cryo Damage and Burst Damage bonuses without needing the Frozen or Burst-buff condition, and it works while you farm either 4-piece.

artifacts.name: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
artifacts.why: Support option that gives an unconditional 12% damage bonus to the element your party is reacting with. The 2-piece also helps her Energy Recharge requirement when a Night Soul Burst triggers in the party.

artifacts.name: Instructor
artifacts.why: Better for Elemental Mastery teams such as Hu Tao Vaporize and Melt, but it costs her the CRIT Rate for her CRIT buff. GameWith uses it for her in the Mavuika Melt team.

buildInfo.dps: Rosaria uses her Skill and Burst to trigger Reverse Melt with a Pyro teammate and stays on the field as the carry. Build Elemental Mastery or Attack, Cryo Damage and CRIT.
buildInfo.subdps: Rosaria stays in the back, applies Cryo for Freeze, Melt and Superconduct, and her Burst gives the team a CRIT Rate buff. Most popular, and it holds most of the top teams.
buildInfo.support: Rosaria gives the party 15% of her CRIT Rate and constant Cryo. Reach 100% CRIT Rate and enough Energy Recharge to cast her Burst on cooldown.

info.role: Cryo Sub DPS or support (Freeze, Superconduct, Melt)

builds/rosaria.name: Rosaria
builds/rosaria.source: Researched 2026-11-12 from GenshinBuilds (v7.2: weapons, artifacts, stats, talent order, teams, community usage), Game8 (weapons, artifacts, stats, talent order, teams) and GameWith (team builds, rotations, substitutes). Rosaria is a 4-star Cryo Polearm character. The guides disagree on substat order (GenshinBuilds' build page lists Energy Recharge first, its team entries list CRIT DMG first). No source gives talent levels, so the level field says so. A fourth page (genshin-build.com) only named Engulfing Lightning with an Attack set and no ranking, so it was used for passives and talent numbers only. theclick.gg could not be reached, and Rosaria is not in GameWith's Mitya Stellar-Conduct teams, so none are listed. White Tassel is the only 3-star named, from community usage.

stats.circlet: CRIT Rate / CRIT DMG
stats.goblet: Cryo DMG Bonus
stats.sands: ATK% or Energy Recharge%
stats.substats: Energy Recharge > CRIT Rate > CRIT DMG > ATK%. GenshinBuilds' team entries list CRIT DMG > CRIT Rate > ATK% > Energy Recharge instead. Targets: 100% CRIT Rate gives the party the full 15% CRIT buff (Game8). Energy Recharge enough to cast her Burst (60 Energy) every rotation, no number given. GenshinBuilds assumes 120% in its Freeze calculations, and Emblem of Severed Fate can overtake Gilded Dreams at 130% or more

dps.substats: Energy Recharge > CRIT Rate > CRIT DMG > Elemental Mastery > ATK% (GenshinBuilds). No numeric targets are listed

subdps.substats: Energy Recharge > CRIT Rate > CRIT DMG > ATK%. GenshinBuilds' team entries list CRIT DMG > CRIT Rate > ATK% > Energy Recharge instead. Targets: 100% CRIT Rate gives the party the full 15% CRIT buff (Game8). Energy Recharge enough to cast her Burst (60 Energy) every rotation, no number given. GenshinBuilds assumes 120% in its Freeze calculations, and Emblem of Severed Fate can overtake Gilded Dreams at 130% or more

support.substats: Energy Recharge > CRIT Rate > CRIT DMG > ATK%. Targets: 100% CRIT Rate for the full 15% party CRIT buff, and enough Energy Recharge to cast her Burst on cooldown, no number given

talents.name: Elemental Burst: Rites of Termination
talents.why: Top priority in both guides, because she casts it in every role. It deals most of her damage as a Sub DPS and gives nearby party members 15% of her CRIT Rate for 10 seconds.

talents.name: Elemental Skill: Ravaging Confession
talents.why: Second for Sub DPS and support builds. GenshinBuilds says to cast it before the Burst, because the +12% CRIT Rate from her Ascension 1 passive also counts toward the Ascension 4 party buff. For Reverse Melt, the Skill and Burst are what trigger Reverse Melt.

talents.name: Normal Attack: Spear of the Church
talents.why: Lowest priority for Sub DPS and support builds. Game8 makes it the top priority only for a Main DPS or Physical Rosaria.

teams.name: Eula Superconduct
teams.note: Rated S by GenshinBuilds. Eula is the Cryo carry, and Raiden's Electro with Rosaria's Cryo triggers Superconduct, which her Burst scales with. Zhongli's shield and Tenacity of the Millelith add Attack. GameWith lists it as her Physical team, where Rosaria's Cryo application is enough to trigger Superconduct, and at C6 she lowers enemy Physical RES by 20%.

teams.name: Hu Tao Melt Vaporize
teams.note: Rated S by GenshinBuilds. Rosaria's Cryo and Xingqiu's Hydro let Hu Tao trigger Melt and Vaporize, and Zhongli's shield protects the team and adds Attack.

teams.name: Mavuika Melt
teams.note: Rated best by GameWith. Mavuika is the slow Pyro carry and can use less CRIT Rate because of Rosaria's buff. Arlecchino or Hu Tao can replace Mavuika, Kazuha, Sucrose or Zhongli can replace Xilonen, and Bennett or Furina can replace Iansan. Rotation: Mavuika Skill, Xilonen Skill and 2 Normal Attacks, Rosaria Skill and Burst, Iansan Skill, 1 Normal Attack and Burst, then Mavuika Burst.

teams.name: Skirk Freeze
teams.note: Rated second by GameWith. Rosaria's Cryo application helps trigger Freeze and she regains Energy easily. Skirk and Escoffier need a team made only of Hydro and Cryo characters. Ayaka or Wriothesley can replace Skirk, Yelan, Xingqiu or Kokomi can replace Furina, and Shenhe, Diona or Charlotte can replace Escoffier.

teams.name: Ayaka Permafrost
teams.note: Rated S by GenshinBuilds. Ayaka and Rosaria both apply Cryo, and Kokomi's off-field Hydro keeps enemies frozen. Kazuha groups enemies and lowers Cryo RES to boost Ayaka's Burst.

teams.name: Arlecchino Melt
teams.note: From Game8. Arlecchino triggers Melt consistently because Rosaria's Cryo application is slow, and Bennett adds the damage buff, Pyro aura and healing. Jean and Bennett together enable Sunfire.

teams.name: Rosaria Melt (on-field)
teams.note: Rated S by GenshinBuilds. Chongyun's Skill infuses Rosaria's attacks with Cryo to trigger Melt, Bennett's Burst boosts those Melt hits, and Kazuha groups enemies and lowers resistances. Game8 also lists Shenhe, Rosaria, Nahida or Kazuha, and Bennett.

teams.name: Rosaria Permafrost Freeze
teams.note: Rated S by GenshinBuilds. Xingqiu's Hydro Burst and Rosaria's Cryo attacks trigger Freeze, Chongyun adds Cryo infusion and cooldown reduction, and Diona's shield and healing keep the rotation stable.

weapons.name: Staff of the Scarlet Sands
weapons.why: Best in slot for the Reverse Melt build in both guides. Base Attack 542 and a 44.1% CRIT Rate substat. It turns 52% of her Elemental Mastery into Attack, and Skill hits add up to 3 stacks of 28% Elemental Mastery as Attack for 10 seconds.

weapons.name: Staff of Homa
weapons.why: Top pick for Freeze teams and a strong Reverse Melt weapon. Base Attack 608 and a 66.2% CRIT Damage substat. It adds 20% HP, plus Attack equal to 0.8% of max HP, and 1% more when her HP is below 50%.

weapons.name: Crimson Moon's Semblance
weapons.why: Second in GenshinBuilds' Reverse Melt list. CRIT Rate substat, and its self-buff keeps working while she is off-field, which fits her quickswap play.

weapons.name: Primordial Jade Winged-Spear
weapons.why: CRIT Rate substat and a passive that stacks Attack and damage while she is on the field. GenshinBuilds assumes about 3 stacks in Reverse Melt and 2 in Freeze, so it is weaker if she is often off-field.

weapons.name: Calamity Queller
weapons.why: Attack% substat and a damage bonus that grows every second she stays on the field. GenshinBuilds counts it at max stacks and does not double its passive.

weapons.name: Deathmatch
weapons.why: The best 4-star for Reverse Melt. Base Attack 454 and a 36.8% CRIT Rate substat. It gives +16% Attack and Defense with 2 or more enemies nearby, or +24% Attack with fewer. GenshinBuilds says that with Gilded Dreams it beats every 4-star option and even Primordial Jade Winged-Spear on a single target.

weapons.name: Favonius Lance
weapons.why: Best when the team has Energy Recharge problems, since her Burst costs 60 Energy. It is also the most used weapon in showcased builds (21%) and GameWith's pick for her Melt and Physical teams. Without energy problems, use a CRIT Rate weapon to get the most from her CRIT buff.

weapons.name: The Catch
weapons.why: Best easy-to-obtain option per Game8. Base Attack 510 and a 45.9% Energy Recharge substat, plus +16% Burst Damage and +6% Burst CRIT Rate, which suits a Burst-focused character.

weapons.name: Skyward Spine
weapons.why: Energy Recharge substat and a CRIT Rate buff on Normal Attacks. GenshinBuilds uses it for her in the Hu Tao Melt Vaporize and Eula Superconduct teams.

weapons.name: Dragon's Bane
weapons.why: Elemental Mastery substat and +20% damage against Pyro-affected enemies, which fits a Reverse Melt team. GenshinBuilds says it is slightly better than Calamity Queller at R4 to R5.

weapons.name: Engulfing Lightning
weapons.why: Energy Recharge weapon. GenshinBuilds lists it for Reverse Melt, and a separate guide recommends it for her as a support. Use it when her Burst needs more energy.

weapons.name: Dragonspine Spear
weapons.why: Physical Damage Bonus substat, used for her Physical builds. It is the second most used weapon in showcased builds (16%), so it is a common choice when she plays in Eula's team.

weapons.name: White Tassel
weapons.why: Appears in 6% of showcased builds as a budget option. The sources give no stats or reasons, so treat it as a placeholder while you farm a better 4-star.

artifacts.name: Gilded Dreams
artifacts.why: Best in slot for off-field Mitya per GenshinBuilds. It gives up to 160 Elemental Mastery with two Cryo teammates, which fits his Stellar-Conduct teams.

artifacts.name: Heart of the Furnace
artifacts.why: GameWith lists this as the on-field DPS set. The page doesn't explain why, so check it against your own damage numbers.

artifacts.name: Disenchantment in Deep Shadow
artifacts.why: Alternative for on-field play, and a good option if you lack Gilded Dreams pieces (GenshinBuilds).

artifacts.name: Wanderer's Troupe + Gilded Dreams (Elemental Mastery +80 each)
artifacts.why: An early Elemental Mastery setup until you have farmed a 4-piece set. It keeps your main stats flexible.

buildInfo.dps: Mitya stays on the field as the main damage dealer, with Valeriy shielding and boosting his Electro damage.
buildInfo.subdps: Mitya applies Electro and buffs Elemental Mastery from the back while Sandrone or Cyno deals the damage. Most popular, and it holds the top-rated teams.

info.role: Electro on-field DPS or off-field Sub DPS (Stellar-Conduct)

builds/mitya.name: Mitya
builds/mitya.source: Researched 2026-11-05 from GenshinBuilds (weapons, artifacts, teams), GameWith (build, stat targets, talent priority, teams) and Game8 (Starsealed Edict stats). Icy Veins, Insider Gaming and Mobalytics were not reachable. The guides disagree on the best artifact set and EM targets, so both are listed. No 3-star weapon is named in the sources, and star ratings for Winter's Heavy Heart could not be confirmed, so it is left out.

stats.goblet: Elemental Mastery
stats.sands: Elemental Mastery
stats.substats: On-field: CRIT Rate = CRIT DMG > Elemental Mastery > Energy Recharge. Off-field: Elemental Mastery > CRIT Rate = CRIT DMG > Energy Recharge.

dps.substats: CRIT Rate = CRIT DMG > EM > ER. Targets (GameWith): EM 600-800, CRIT Rate 60-70%+, CRIT DMG 155-180%+, Energy Recharge 100-120%
