talents.name: Normal Attack: Chain Reaction
talents.why: First priority for on-field Mitya in both guides. Off-field builds can ignore it.

talents.name: Elemental Burst: Analysis: Gradient Theory
talents.why: Second priority in GenshinBuilds and 4/5 in both of GameWith's roles.

talents.name: Elemental Skill: Principle: Variable Detection
talents.why: Top priority for the off-field Sub DPS build, since the Skill sets which role he plays. GenshinBuilds ranks it last.

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct (Sandrone)
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds. Sandrone is the on-field Cryo main DPS, Mitya applies Electro off-field, Odette converts reactions, and Alyosha buffs and heals.

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct (Cyno)
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds. Cyno's Electro-infused attacks combine with Odette's Cryo-to-Stellar conversion and Mitya's off-field Electro application.

teams.name: Off-field Stellar-Conduct
teams.note: Rated 5 stars by GameWith. Mitya deals Stellar-Conduct damage off-field, Odette boosts Stellar Glimmer damage and Yae Miko adds steady Electro. Her quest must be done for her Stellar-Conduct buffs.

teams.name: On-field Mitya
teams.note: Rated 4 stars by GameWith. Valeriy shields the team and boosts Mitya's Electro damage. Fischl can replace Yae Miko.

teams.name: Budget Mitya
teams.note: Rated 3 stars by GameWith. Built from 4-star characters. Valeriy and Diona shield him and keep Stellar-Conduct going, and Sucrose boosts his Elemental Mastery.

weapons.name: Starsealed Edict
weapons.why: His signature weapon and best in slot. It gives CRIT DMG (88.2% at Lv. 90) and a passive with Elemental Mastery stacks that last while he is off-field. His normal combo triggers all three buffs, and the passive also raises his Stellar-Conduct CRIT DMG. GameWith rates it DPS SS.

weapons.name: Reliquary of Truth
weapons.why: A big CRIT DMG stat stick. Reliable for on-field Mitya, though he can't use its other passive effects fully.

weapons.name: Sunny Morning Sleep-In
weapons.why: Gives a large amount of Elemental Mastery (265 at Lv. 90) and more after his Skill, which boosts his Stellar-Conduct damage.

weapons.name: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds
weapons.why: High CRIT Rate substat and an Elemental Damage bonus that stacks, which fits his damage.

weapons.name: Dawning Frost
weapons.why: CRIT DMG substat. Its passive alternates Elemental Mastery and CRIT buffs, and Mitya triggers both in a single combo (GenshinBuilds).

weapons.name: The Widsith
weapons.why: CRIT DMG substat with random buffs that include Elemental Mastery. High Elemental Mastery uptime makes it a solid 4-star option.

weapons.name: Wandering Evenstar
weapons.why: Elemental Mastery substat and bonus Damage against Electro-affected enemies. GameWith lists it for on-field builds, at R5, paired with an Attack scaler.

weapons.name: Etherlight Spindlelute
weapons.why: Energy Recharge substat that solves his Energy Recharge issues. It is an event weapon, so check whether you already own it.

artifacts.name: Golden Troupe
artifacts.why: Her best set for personal damage. The 4-piece boosts her Elemental Skill damage, with an even bigger bonus while she is off-field, which is where she spends most of her time. Used on about 83% of profiles.

artifacts.name: Tenacity of the Millelith
artifacts.why: Often the best pick when she is a buffer. When her Skill hits, the team gets an Attack buff and a shield. She keeps it active easily. Choose it when your damage dealer can't use the set themselves.

artifacts.name: Emblem of Severed Fate
artifacts.why: Boosts Hydro damage with an extra bonus after her Skill. Best for pure damage builds, especially if Energy Recharge is already covered.

artifacts.name: Golden Troupe (Skill DMG +20%) + Tenacity of the Millelith (HP +20%)
artifacts.why: The flexible mix. You keep the Skill damage and HP scaling for her, and it frees up main stats and substats.

artifacts.name: Tenacity of the Millelith (HP +20%) + Emblem of Severed Fate (Energy Recharge +20%)
artifacts.why: Good when you need Energy Recharge fast. HP scaling for her Salon Members plus extra Energy Recharge for her Burst uptime.

info.role: Hydro off-field support and buffer (or Hydro sub DPS / main DPS)

builds/furina.name: Furina
builds/furina.source: Researched 2026-10-31 from Icy Veins (Furina guide, Energy Recharge targets and teams), GenshinBuilds (weapons, artifacts, teams) and Prydwen (weapon notes, rotation, HP target). Furina needs a healer in her team: her Salon Members lose damage when teammates drop to 50% HP. Re-checked 2026-11-11 against Icy Veins (updated for 7.2 on 3 Nov 2026) and GenshinBuilds (v7.2): Energy Recharge and stat targets updated.

stats.circlet: CRIT Rate or CRIT DMG
stats.goblet: HP% (easier to farm, great with Golden Troupe) or Hydro DMG% (only slightly worse, best when she gets few Damage buffs)
stats.sands: Energy Recharge (when needed) or HP%
stats.substats: Energy Recharge (until target) > CRIT Rate > CRIT DMG > HP% > HP. Energy Recharge targets (Icy Veins, 7.2): about 160-180%+ in a standard team, 140-160% with a second Hydro teammate, 110-130% in a Neuvillette team, and 180-200%+ for high-energy content or Stygian Onslaught. At C4+ these requirements drop by about 40%. A Favonius weapon lowers them further. Stat targets: about 33,000-40,000+ HP, about 70% CRIT Rate and 140%+ CRIT DMG. HP is useful because her second Ascension Talent maxes out at 40,000 Max HP.

talents.name: Elemental Burst: Let the People Rejoice
talents.why: First priority in every guide. It sets her Fanfare buff and the size of the team damage boost.

talents.name: Elemental Skill: Salon Solitaire
talents.why: Second priority. It controls her Salon Members and Hydro application, which is most of her off-field damage.

talents.name: Normal Attack: Solitary Suffusion
talents.why: Last priority. Her Normal and Charged Attacks are weak and are mostly used to trigger weapon passives.

teams.name: Neuvillette hypercarry
teams.note: A top team. Furina buffs Neuvillette's Charged Attacks while Fischl adds off-field Electro. Jean or Kazuha can give Anemo RES shred, and Baizhu is an alternative healer.

teams.name: Skirk freeze
teams.note: Skirk is the Cryo main DPS and Escoffier shreds Cryo and Hydro RES. Furina and Mona supply Hydro and buffs. Lunar and Stellar teams don't use her damage bonus buffs, but Freedom-Sworn fits here.

teams.name: Hyperbloom / Aggravate
teams.note: Clorinde's Electro triggers Aggravate and Hyperbloom, Furina gives off-field Hydro, and Nahida applies Dendro. Baizhu keeps the team alive.

teams.name: Bloom (Neuvillette)
teams.note: Hydro from Neuvillette and Furina forms Bloom cores. Kazuha groups enemies and buffs damage, and Baizhu heals.

teams.name: Vaporize (Hu Tao)
teams.note: Yelan and Furina apply Hydro off-field for Hu Tao's Vaporize. Bennett or Xianyun can replace Zhongli as healer, which changes Hu Tao's play style.

teams.name: Raiden Electro-Charged
teams.note: Yelan and Furina supply Hydro for Electro-Charged. Jean heals to support Furina's HP-based Burst.

teams.name: Furina Bloom (main DPS)
teams.note: Nilou's passive turns Bloom cores into Bountiful Cores for big area damage. Furina is the on-field Hydro driver here.

teams.name: Furina Vaporize (main DPS)
teams.note: Xiangling supplies Pyro for Vaporize. Bennett's healing supports Furina's HP drain.

teams.name: Xiao hypercarry
teams.note: Boosts Xiao's Anemo damage. Xianyun has strong synergy with Furina.

teams.name: Quickbloom
teams.note: Furina's Hydro and Emilie's Dendro form Bloom cores, which Raiden's Skill detonates as Hyperbloom.

weapons.name: Splendor of Tranquil Waters
weapons.why: Her signature weapon and the best pick for her own damage. It gives Crit Damage, and its passive raises her Skill damage and Max HP, which fits how her Salon Members and Fanfare scale. It is worth running even if it means taking an Energy Recharge Sands.

weapons.name: Favonius Sword
weapons.why: Often the strongest practical option. The Energy Recharge substat and the extra particles help Furina and the whole team, and her Energy Recharge needs are high. It also lowers your Energy Recharge target by about 10%.

weapons.name: Key of Khaj-Nisut
weapons.why: HP% substat boosts her own damage, and its passive turns her HP into a team Elemental Mastery buff. This often makes it her best choice in Vaporize and Lunar teams.

weapons.name: Primordial Jade Cutter
weapons.why: Strong Crit Rate substat and a passive that converts Max HP into Attack, which stacks quickly on an HP-scaling character. Best for raw personal damage.

weapons.name: Festering Desire
weapons.why: Easy to obtain. It gives Energy Recharge, plus Skill damage and Skill Crit Rate, so it works well for her Skill-focused kit. Icy Veins notes it was an event-exclusive weapon that can no longer be obtained, so it only applies if you already own it.

weapons.name: Fleuve Cendre Ferryman
weapons.why: Easy to obtain through fishing. Energy Recharge substat and Skill-related buffs make it a solid budget pick.

weapons.name: Freedom-Sworn
weapons.why: A supportive pick when your damage dealer benefits from its team buff and her Energy Recharge needs are already met, such as on Skirk teams.

weapons.name: Serenity's Call
weapons.why: Easy to obtain. Gives Energy Recharge and works well for personal damage and energy when the passive is fully active at higher refinements.

weapons.name: Wolf-Fang
weapons.why: Battle Pass sword with a Crit Rate substat. It can outperform Serenity's Call when her Energy Recharge is low, and suits Skill-heavy rotations.

weapons.name: Uraku Misugiri
weapons.why: Crit Damage substat with Skill and Normal Attack damage buffs. Best when you have no Geo teammate and want personal damage.

weapons.name: Haran Geppaku Futsu
weapons.why: Normal Attacks stack Elemental Damage, which suits brief on-field phases. A niche pick for Furina as a damage dealer.

weapons.name: Light of Foliar Incision
weapons.why: Only worth it in Vaporize or Hyperbloom teams where Elemental Mastery matters. Not a general pick.

weapons.name: The Dockhand's Assistant
weapons.why: HP% substat with an Attack buff when she is healed. Pairs well with a team-wide healer, but is not the first choice.

weapons.name: Harbinger of Dawn
weapons.why: A 3-star Crit Damage option. It needs a strong healer to keep its passive active, so treat it as a budget stopgap.

artifacts.name: Noblesse Oblige
artifacts.why: The default support set. His Burst already gives Attack, and this set gives the whole party 20 percent Attack for 12 seconds after the Burst. It does not stack with another Noblesse Oblige, so use it when nobody else in the team provides it.

artifacts.name: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
artifacts.why: Gives the party 12 percent Elemental Damage Bonus after reactions. Best when a teammate already wears Noblesse Oblige, and the alternative GameWith names.

artifacts.name: Instructor
artifacts.why: Gives the party 120 Elemental Mastery after a reaction, so it suits reaction teams that value Elemental Mastery over Attack percent.

artifacts.name: Deepwood Memories
artifacts.why: Lowers enemy Dendro Resistance by 30 percent after Skill or Burst hits. Best for Dendro damage teams.

buildInfo.support: Bennett heals and gives the party a flat Attack buff with his Burst. The buff scales only off his and his weapon's base Attack, so external Attack percent does not raise it. Build Energy Recharge first, then HP percent and Crit Rate.

builds/bennett.name: Bennett
builds/bennett.source: Researched 2026-11-14 from GenshinBuilds (weapons, artifacts, teams, talent order, showcase data) and GameWith (weapon notes, Energy Recharge targets, talent order, teams), and Icy Veins (roles and Energy Recharge ranges). Icy Veins' artifact and substat tables were empty and its pages for teams could not be fully read. GameWith's page was only partly retrievable. The guides disagree on the best weapon (Skyward Blade vs Mistsplitter Reforged) and on the exact Energy Recharge target. No 3-star weapon is named in the sources. GenshinBuilds also lists a separate DPS build (Crimson Witch of Flames, Thundering Fury, Marechaussee Hunter with Furina) without explaining it, so it is not included.

stats.circlet: CRIT Rate, HP% or Healing Bonus
stats.goblet: HP% or Pyro DMG Bonus
stats.sands: Energy Recharge% or HP%
stats.substats: Energy Recharge > CRIT Rate > HP% > ATK% per GenshinBuilds, and Energy Recharge > HP% > CRIT Rate (with Favonius Sword) per GameWith. Energy Recharge targets (GameWith): 200 to 250% with no other Pyro teammate, 180 to 220% with one other Pyro, 165 to 190% with two other Pyro. Another guide lists about 150 to 200% with two Pyro characters and about 250% alone. CRIT Rate at least 80% if using Favonius Sword

talents.name: Elemental Burst: Fantastic Voyage
talents.why: Top priority in every guide. It heals, and its Attack buff is the reason he is in the team.

talents.name: Elemental Skill: Passion Overload
talents.why: Second priority in every guide that lists one. It applies Pyro and creates Energy Particles, which helps his Energy Recharge needs.

talents.name: Normal Attack: Strike of Fortune
talents.why: Lowest priority. One guide says Normal Attacks can be ignored.

teams.name: Vaporize (Tartaglia)
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds. Tartaglia is the Hydro carry, Xiangling applies off-field Pyro for Vaporize, Kazuha shreds resistance and groups enemies, and Bennett heals and buffs Attack. Gear: Skyward Blade or Favonius Sword with Noblesse Oblige on Bennett.

teams.name: Thunder (Raiden)
teams.note: Rated SS by GenshinBuilds. Sara's C6 adds Electro Crit Damage to Raiden's Burst, Kazuha adds a damage buff and resistance shred, and Bennett's Attack buff supports the Burst.

teams.name: National (Raiden)
teams.note: GameWith's strongest variant of the National team. Bennett gives Pyro resonance and healing, Xiangling covers Pyro, and Xingqiu applies Hydro.

teams.name: International (Tartaglia)
teams.note: A GameWith variant that replaces Xingqiu with Sucrose. Sucrose adds Elemental Mastery and groups enemies, while Bennett and Xiangling cover Pyro and healing.

teams.name: Melt (Ganyu)
teams.note: Bennett supplies Pyro application and buffs for Melt, and Zhongli adds a shield. A GameWith team.

teams.name: Hypercarry (Wanderer)
teams.note: Faruzan boosts Anemo damage, Layla shields, and Bennett heals and buffs Attack. A GameWith team.

teams.name: Pyro with Mavuika
teams.note: The team GameWith recommends for the Noblesse Oblige build. The full team notes were not retrievable.

weapons.name: Skyward Blade
weapons.why: GameWith's best pick. Its Energy Recharge secondary stat helps him reach his Energy Recharge target without leaning on artifacts. GenshinBuilds adds that it keeps Burst uptime reliable and gives Crit Rate and attack speed after the Burst.

weapons.name: Mistsplitter Reforged
weapons.why: Best in slot in two guides. It has high base Attack, which his Burst buff scales with, and its passive stacks Elemental Damage Bonus after the Burst. It pays off only if he does real off-field damage, and it gives no Energy Recharge.

weapons.name: Absolution
weapons.why: Limited 5-star with 674 base Attack, the highest on the list. It raises his Attack after the Skill and has a Crit Damage stat. Use it when his artifacts already cover Energy Recharge.

weapons.name: Azurelight
weapons.why: Limited 5-star with 674 base Attack and a Crit Rate stat. Its Skill-triggered Attack bonus ramps before damage windows. Use it when his artifacts supply enough Energy Recharge.

weapons.name: Sapwood Blade
weapons.why: Best free-to-play pick in GameWith. It is craftable, has relatively high base Attack for a 4-star, and gives Energy Recharge. Its Burst-triggered reaction passive gives the party 60 Elemental Mastery, which suits Hyperbloom or Spread teams.

weapons.name: Favonius Sword
weapons.why: A reliable Energy fix with Energy Particles for the team. It is the most used weapon on his showcase data (22 percent). The low base Attack makes his Burst buff weaker, and GameWith wants at least 80 percent Crit Rate with it.

weapons.name: Prototype Rancour
weapons.why: Craftable and self-sufficient. It gives Attack and a Physical Damage Bonus, so it is the second free-to-play option after Sapwood Blade.

weapons.name: Freedom-Sworn
weapons.why: Its Sigil passive gives the party 20 percent Attack and 16 percent Normal, Charged and Plunging Damage. GameWith says it works best when he triggers two reactions per rotation, which is hard to do reliably.

weapons.name: Aquila Favonia
weapons.why: Highest-tier base Attack (674), so his Burst buff gets stronger. The Physical Damage Bonus and passive do little for a support, so take it only if you lack Energy Recharge or utility swords.

weapons.name: The Alley Flash
weapons.why: Highest 4-star base Attack with an Elemental Mastery stat. A cheap pick for reaction teams, but it gives no Energy Recharge.

weapons.name: Peak Patrol Song
weapons.why: Passes Elemental Damage Bonus to party members, which makes it competitive for teams built around Damage Bonus. It gives Defense instead of Energy Recharge.

weapons.name: Calamity of Eshu
weapons.why: Attack stat stick. Its passive needs a shielder to add Normal and Charged Attack damage, so for him it is mostly a stat option.

artifacts.name: Night of the Sky's Unveiling
artifacts.why: Best set in both guides. The 2-piece gives +80 Elemental Mastery. The 4-piece gives her a 4-second buff when nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions: more CRIT Rate at the Nascent or Ascendant Gleam Moonsign levels, plus more Lunar Reaction Damage for the whole party.

artifacts.name: Husk of Opulent Dreams
artifacts.why: A DEF-scaling alternative. The 2-piece gives +30% DEF and the 4-piece stacks DEF and Geo Damage Bonus. Listed by GenshinBuilds.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: Night of the Sky's Unveiling (EM +80), Wanderer's Troupe (EM +80) or Husk of Opulent Dreams (DEF +30%)
artifacts.why: Mixing two 2-pieces is a community build on GenshinBuilds, using Night of the Sky's Unveiling or Gladiator's Finale with Wanderer's Troupe. Gladiator's Finale only adds Attack +18%, which is of little use to a DEF-scaling character, so I would pick Elemental Mastery or DEF pieces instead.

builds/zibai.name: Zibai

weapons.name: Lightbearing Moonshard
weapons.why: Her signature weapon and best in slot in both guides. It adds DEF and boosts Lunar-Crystallize Damage for a short time after her Elemental Skill.

weapons.name: Uraku Misugiri
weapons.why: High CRIT Damage, and it converts DEF into Elemental Skill and Normal Attack Damage. Both guides rank it second and say it pairs with DEF-stacking artifacts.

weapons.name: Light of Foliar Incision
weapons.why: Gives CRIT Rate and a passive that scales her Normal Attack and Skill Damage with Elemental Mastery.

weapons.name: Peak Patrol Song
weapons.why: Large DEF from its main stat and passive. Icy Veins says it beats most free-to-play options on raw stats, but its Damage bonus is weak.

weapons.why: High CRIT Damage as a stat stick. Its passive favors HP scaling, so use it only if you need it.

weapons.name: Flute of Ezpitzal

weapons.name: Cinnabar Spindle
weapons.why: Adds Elemental Skill Damage based on DEF. Listed by Icy Veins as a 4-star option.

weapons.name: Harbinger of Dawn
weapons.why: A budget CRIT option, and a 3-star you can get free from story quests or any banner. Its bonus needs HP above 90%, so it works best with a shielder. Icy Veins notes the CRIT Rate can overcap.

weapons.name: Haran Geppaku Futsu

weapons.name: Xiphos' Moonlight
weapons.why: Adds Elemental Mastery and Energy Recharge through its passive. Listed by Icy Veins.

weapons.name: Athame Artis
weapons.why: Durin's signature weapon (Icy Veins lists it as 5-star). GenshinBuilds lists it as a budget reaction sword for Zibai that grants Attack and Elemental Mastery after Lunar-Crystallize.

artifacts.name: Heart of the Furnace
artifacts.why: Best in slot. The 2-piece gives +18% Attack. The 4-piece gives +12% Attack when she triggers or deals Stellar Glimmer reaction damage, and raises the team's Stellar Glimmer reaction Damage by 50%, even while she is off-field. It does not stack, so only she needs it.

artifacts.name: Disenchantment in Deep Shadow
artifacts.why: The best pick in Stellar-Conduct teams when a teammate already uses Heart of the Furnace. It boosts Stellar-Conduct Damage by 40% and gives CRIT Rate against affected enemies. It adds nothing in Stellar-Swirl teams.

artifacts.name: Tenacity of the Millelith
artifacts.why: Better when buffing the team matters more than her own Damage, especially for Attack-scaling carries nobody else is buffing. Also useful until you farm Heart of the Furnace.

artifacts.name: Viridescent Venerer
artifacts.why: Useful in Stellar-Swirl teams for its Resistance shred. Use it only if no teammate already wears it. Icy Veins lists it after Tenacity of the Millelith.

artifacts.name: 2pc mix: Gladiator's Finale (Attack +18%) with A Day Carved From Rising Winds (Attack +18%)
artifacts.why: A simple Attack percent mix to use while you farm a 4-piece set. Any two sets that each give Attack percent work.

builds/odette.name: Odette
builds/odette.source: Several Odette build guides for version 7.1 (GenshinBuilds, AllThings.how, Beebom and TimeSaver). They agree on Whitelake Frostfeather, Heart of the Furnace, Attack percent Sands and Goblet, and a CRIT Rate or CRIT Damage Circlet. Sources disagree on the exact Attack targets (about 2,000 for the team bonus and 3,000 for her personal bonus, with about 2,500 realistic), and one source puts Elemental Mastery above Energy Recharge while another skips Energy Recharge. Weapon star ratings for Absolution, The Alley Flash, Xiphos' Moonlight and Harbinger of Dawn are from my own knowledge. Team ratings come from one guide, and Stellar Swirl numbers from before September 23 may be understated.

stats.circlet: CRIT Rate or CRIT Damage (her ascension already gives CRIT Damage, so CRIT Rate often balances her better)
stats.goblet: Attack% (Elemental Mastery once Attack is high). Cryo Damage% does not affect her reaction Damage
stats.sands: Attack% (Elemental Mastery once Attack is high)
stats.substats: CRIT Rate = CRIT Damage > Attack% > Elemental Mastery > Energy Recharge. Energy Recharge can usually be skipped because she rarely casts her Burst. Targets (Icy Veins): HP 17,000 to 20,000, Attack 2,400 to 2,600 (about 3,000 with Attack% buffs), CRIT Rate 60 to 75%, CRIT Damage 150 to 175%, Energy Recharge 100 to 130%. Past 2,000 Attack, extra Attack mostly helps her own Damage, so put the rest into CRIT if you play her as a support.

talents.name: Elemental Skill
talents.why: Top priority. It summons the dance double that deals off-field Cryo Damage and drives most of her reactions and Damage.

talents.name: Elemental Burst
talents.why: Second priority. It is usually not worth casting before C4, so level it only if you plan to cast it.

talents.name: Normal Attack
talents.why: Leave it at level 1. She rarely attacks on the field.

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct: Sandrone, Yae Miko, Alyosha (SS)

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct: Sandrone, Qiqi, Alyosha (SS)

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct: Cyno, Yae Miko, Alyosha

teams.name: Stellar-Conduct: Wriothesley, Yae Miko, Nicole

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Yumemizuki Mizuki, Qiqi, Sucrose

teams.name: Stellar-Swirl: Yumemizuki Mizuki, Cryo Traveler, Sucrose

teams.name: Accessible Cryo and Electro: Fischl, Beidou, Cryo Traveler
teams.note: A lower-investment team that uses characters most players already have.

weapons.name: Whitelake Frostfeather
weapons.why: Her signature weapon and best in slot. It has high base Attack and a CRIT Rate substat. Skill hits stack Attack, and at 3 stacks it boosts the CRIT Damage of her Stellar Glimmer reactions and restores Energy off-field.

weapons.name: Azurelight

artifacts.why: Required in most Dendro reaction teams. The 2-piece gives +15% Dendro Damage. The 4-piece lowers Dendro RES by 30% for 8 seconds after a Skill or Burst hit, even off-field. Lauma or a teammate with high Skill uptime can hold it.

artifacts.name: Gilded Dreams
artifacts.why: For high Elemental Mastery builds. The 2-piece gives +80 Elemental Mastery. The 4-piece gives Attack and Elemental Mastery after a reaction. Best when teammates already hold the best support sets.

artifacts.why: Only for teams in Ascendant Gleam where Lauma does much of the team's Damage. It adds Energy Recharge and Elemental Mastery for an on-field Lauma.

builds/lauma.name: Lauma
builds/lauma.source: Several Lauma build guides: Icy Veins (updated for 6.3), GenshinBuilds (v7.1) and KeqingMains (Luna V quick guide). They agree on Nightweaver's Looking Glass, Silken Moon's Serenade and Deepwood Memories, Elemental Mastery on Goblet and Circlet, and Lunar-Bloom as her best archetype. They disagree on the talent order (Icy Veins puts the Skill first, GenshinBuilds the Burst first, KeqingMains calls both the priority) and on substat order (Elemental Mastery first in one guide, Energy Recharge first in two). Icy Veins did not label the rarity of Starcaller's Watch or Sunny Morning Sleep-In, so I used KeqingMains' 5-star label, which may be wrong. Wandering Evenstar's rarity is from my own knowledge. Targets assume decent artifacts and Etherlight Spindlelute.

stats.circlet: Elemental Mastery (CRIT Rate or CRIT Damage if she deals a lot of personal Damage)
stats.goblet: Elemental Mastery
stats.sands: Elemental Mastery or Energy Recharge (Energy Recharge if your weapon gives no Energy)
stats.substats: Energy Recharge first, until you reach her requirement. Then Elemental Mastery, which stays the top priority after that. Then CRIT Rate and CRIT Damage, which matter more in teams where she deals a lot of Damage herself. Energy Recharge 170 to 200% (about 125 to 155% at C4 in a solo Dendro team). Targets: HP 18,000 to 20,000, Attack 1,200, CRIT Rate 40 to 60%, CRIT Damage 130 to 160%, Elemental Mastery 900 to 1,100.

artifacts.name: Noblesse Oblige

artifacts.name: Emblem of Severed Fate

artifacts.name: Nymph's Dream

artifacts.name: Tenacity of the Millelith

artifacts.name: Instructor
artifacts.why: Gives the team an EM buff after the wearer triggers a reaction on field. A highly recommended set when she is the Hydro applicator in a bloom-based reaction team and no one else holds the set.

scripts/request.script:
[LANDSCAPE 16:9 FULL CHARACTER GUIDE: VALERIY. Estimated narration: about 17 minutes. Eight chapters. Every part has a [Start ...] and [End ...] trigger. Kit numbers come from version 7.2 data, so they can still change.]

[0s-62s CHAPTER 1: CHARACTER INTRODUCTION & PULL VALUE]
[Start Introduction]
One 4-star Electro shield can lift the damage of a whole Stellar-Conduct team, and most players never build him for it. Stay to the end and you will know which weapon, artifacts and teams make Valeriy worth your time, and whether he deserves a spot on your account.

Valeriy is a 4-star Electro Sword user who plays as a support. His Elemental Skill puts a long Electro shield on the active character, and the shield strength scales with his Attack. His Burst calls down Thunderburst Shells that hit enemies in an area. Between those two, he protects your carry and feeds the team Attack-based buffs.

His home is Stellar-Conduct teams. When a party member triggers Superconduct, it turns into Stellar-Conduct inside a Polestar Field, and Valeriy boosts that Electro damage. That is why he pairs so well with Mitya, Odette and Cyno.

What he does well is simple. He gives you a strong shield and buffs that reach the whole team, and his 4-star rarity makes him easy to obtain and easy to build. Where he falls short is just as clear, because he needs Stellar-Conduct or Electro teams to shine and does little on his own. Pull or build him if you run Mitya, Cyno or Odette, or if you want a shield support for Clorinde. Valeriy debuted in version 7.2, so some rankings can still shift after more testing.
[End Introduction]

[62s-74s CHAPTER 1: CONSTELLATIONS]
[Start Constellations]
Constellations decide how far you push him, and each level does something different. Before we go through them one by one, here is what you need to know.

Constellations are the upgrades you unlock by pulling duplicates of Valeriy, one level per duplicate, up to a maximum of six. You do not need any of them to use him. Everything in this guide works at Constellation 0, and he is a perfectly good shield and buff support without a single one. But his constellations are worth knowing, because they change how much he gives your team.

Generally speaking, they fall into three groups. Constellation 1 and Constellation 4 improve his Charged Attack and his Energy, so they help his own rotation. Constellation 3 and Constellation 5 raise his Normal Attack and Elemental Skill levels, so they make the talents you already level stronger. And Constellation 2 and Constellation 6 are the two that buff the team, which means those are the ones that matter most for how good he is next to Mitya, Cyno or Clorinde.

Constellation 2 is the biggest jump. It gives nearby party members 100 Elemental Mastery and turns extra Impact Momentum into shield strength, so it is the first one worth aiming for. Constellation 6 is the strongest overall, adding 100 percent damage to his special Charged Attack and his Thunderburst Shells, plus extra Electro Crit Rate and Crit Damage on enemies he hits. Since he is a 4-star, he is easier to get duplicates for than a 5-star, so reaching Constellation 2 is realistic for most players.

Keep in mind that these numbers come from version 7.2 data, so check them in game. Here is what each constellation gives you, in order.
[End Constellations]

[74s-93s CHAPTER 1: CONSTELLATION 1]
[Start Constellation 1]
The first constellation is all about Energy, and that matters because Valeriy's Burst costs 60 Energy, which is a lot for a support. Without help, he needs a good amount of Energy Recharge or a teammate who feeds him particles before he can use it every rotation. Constellation 1 fixes much of that problem from inside his own kit. It also makes his special Charged Attack easier to reach, so his shield and buffs come online sooner at the start of a fight. That makes it a quiet but useful upgrade, and the first step toward the bigger team buffs that come later.

Constellation 1 refunds Energy. After his special Charged Attack, he regains 6 Elemental Energy. If he spends more than 40 Impact Momentum, he gains 1.5 more Energy for every 10 extra points, up to 15 Energy per use, once every 15 seconds. The first Skill of each fight also grants 150 percent Impact Momentum, so his Charged Attack is ready faster.
[End Constellation 1]

[93s-110s CHAPTER 1: CONSTELLATION 2]
[Start Constellation 2]
The biggest jump comes next.

Constellation 2 buffs the team. For 18 seconds after his Skill, nearby party members gain 100 Elemental Mastery. And while he is shielded at maximum Impact Momentum, the extra momentum turns into shield strength, 8 percent of his Attack per point, up to 20 points. This is the biggest jump in his kit.
[End Constellation 2]

[110s-122s CHAPTER 1: CONSTELLATION 3]
[Start Constellation 3]
A simple one, a talent boost.

Constellation 3 raises his Normal Attack by 3 levels, up to a maximum of level 15. Since his Normal Attack is a top talent, this one helps his damage directly.
[End Constellation 3]

[122s-134s CHAPTER 1: CONSTELLATION 4]
[Start Constellation 4]
This one pushes his Charged Attack higher.

Constellation 4 raises his Impact Momentum limit by 30 and his charging efficiency by 30 percent. The maximum momentum he can gain after his Burst also rises to 104, so the Charged Attack gets stronger.
[End Constellation 4]

[134s-146s CHAPTER 1: CONSTELLATION 5]
[Start Constellation 5]
Another talent boost, this time for the shield.

Constellation 5 raises his Elemental Skill by 3 levels, up to a maximum of level 15. A higher Skill level means a stronger shield and stronger buffs.
[End Constellation 5]

[146s-167s CHAPTER 1: CONSTELLATION 6]
[Start Constellation 6]
The last one hits hardest.

Constellation 6 adds 100 percent damage to his special Charged Attack and his Thunderburst Shells. Enemies he hits also take 10 percent more Electro Crit Rate for 7 seconds, and Stellar-Conduct reaction damage from those enemies gains 40 percent Crit Damage.

He works fine at zero constellations, and Constellation 2 gives the biggest jump. These numbers come from version 7.2 data, so check them in game.
[End Constellation 6]

[167s-229s CHAPTER 2: TALENT MECHANICS]
[Start Talent Mechanics]
Level the wrong talent and you waste books. His kit comes first, then the order that pays off.

His Normal Attack is up to three sword strikes. His Charged Attack leaps and slams the ground for Physical area damage. But when he holds at least 40 Impact Momentum, the Charged Attack turns into a special Charged Attack that spends all of it for a bigger hit. That is his damage engine.

His Elemental Skill deals Electro area damage, gives him 40 Impact Momentum, and puts up the Supercharged Shield. The shield strength scales with his Attack, and it absorbs Electro damage at 250 percent efficiency. So a high Attack stat makes the shield sturdier.

His Elemental Burst deals Electro area damage, then fires a Thunderburst Shell that splits into a barrage. While the shells fall, each time a nearby party member hits an enemy with Electro, he gains 5 Impact Momentum, up to 80 per Burst. That means Electro teammates fill his Charged Attack for him.

Two passives matter. Each Impact Momentum he spends on the special Charged Attack raises the damage bonus of his Offensive Directive, by 0.9 percent of his Attack inside Stellar-Conduct and 0.3 percent otherwise. And he enters the Stellar-Conduct state while he stands in a Polestar Field.
[End Talent Mechanics]

[229s-265s CHAPTER 2: TALENT PRIORITY]
[Start Talent Priority]
Here are his talents in order, with the priority of each. The two guides I checked disagree on which comes first, so both views follow.

[Start Elemental Skill 1]
Elemental Skill is the first priority in one guide, because it makes his Attack-scaling shield and his team buffs.
[Start ES Level 9]
Level target: 9 or higher.

[Start Normal Attack 2]
Normal Attack is the second priority here. The other guide puts it first, because it boosts his Offensive Directive buffs and his Charged Attack damage.
[Start NA Level 9]
Level target: 9 or higher.

[Start Elemental Burst 3]
Elemental Burst is the last priority in both guides, since it mainly adds personal damage.
[Start EB Level 1 to 6]
Level target: 1 to 6.

If your books are limited, level both Skill and Normal Attack and leave the Burst low. This is community-tested advice, not a calculated ranking.

[End ES Level 9]
[End NA Level 9]
[End EB Level 1 to 6]
[End Elemental Skill 1]
[End Normal Attack 2]
[End Elemental Burst 3]
[End Talent Priority]

[265s-298s CHAPTER 3: BEST WEAPONS, INTRO]
[Start Weapons Intro]
His best weapon might already sit in your inventory. Twelve options are coming, and the order matters.

Weapons next. I will go through every weapon in his build guide: what it gives him, why it works, where it falls short, and who should use it. Valeriy is a 4-star with no signature weapon, so there is no single must-have pick.

One rule before we start. He scales with Attack, because his shield and buffs scale with Attack, and he also needs enough Energy Recharge to cast his 60 Energy Burst. So every weapon has to pass one check: it gives him Attack or Energy Recharge, and it does not fight his support role.
[End Weapons Intro]

[298s-323s CHAPTER 3: WEAPON 1, SUMMIT SHAPER]
[Start Summit Shaper]
Start with the best stat line in his guide.

[Summit Shaper] Summit Shaper is best in slot in both guides. It has the highest base Attack of the list, 608 at level 90, a 49.6 percent Attack bonus, and a Shield Strength passive that makes his Attack-scaling shield much stronger. Advantage: bigger Attack and a bigger shield, with no setup. Disadvantage: no Energy Recharge, so your artifacts or team must cover his Burst energy. Use it if you own it, because nothing else in the guide beats it.
[End Summit Shaper]

[323s-340s CHAPTER 3: WEAPON 2, FINALE OF THE DEEP]
[Start Finale of the Deep]
The best 4-star for Attack.

Easy to obtain alternatives:
[Start Finale of the Deep]
Finale of the Deep, for Attack.

Favonius Sword, for Energy Recharge.

[Start A Day Carved From Rising Winds]

[End Summit Shaper]
[End Finale of the Deep]

Valeriy.

Mitya.

Odette.

Valeriy.

Build him too if you want a shield for Clorinde in an Overloaded team. As a 4-star, he costs less than most supports, and you can build him with easy to obtain gear.

Skip him if you do not own an Electro carry and do not plan to pull one, because his buffs need Electro damage to matter. Skip him as well if you want a healer, since he shields and does not heal.

updatesum/result.hook: Genshin Impact Version 7.2, Hour of Ruin, is confirmed! Here is everything from the Special Program
updatesum/result.note: Summary of the 7.2 Special Program transcript. No release date was given in the transcript.

sections.body: The Nails of Retribution have triggered the Hallowing, which can reset all of Teyvat. The Archons of all seven nations meet at a summit, and Noy, a fae from the Hyperborea era, joins the fight.
sections.label: Story

sections.body: 5-star Electro Catalyst. He turns Superconduct into Stellar-Conduct, boosts the whole party's Stellar-Conduct Damage, and creates Gradient Beacons. His detection device can follow enemies and deal Damage or support the team.
sections.label: Mitya

sections.body: 4-star Electro support. His shield protects the team, he boosts Electro Damage, and he does even more in Stellar-Conduct teams. His Burst fires artillery shells.
sections.label: Valeriy

sections.body: First half: Mitya, a Furina rerun, Valeriy with a boosted rate, and the 5-star Catalyst Starsealed Edict. Second half: Zibai and Linnea return. A new Chronicled Wish has Varesa, Chasca, Xilonen, Mualani and Kinich.
sections.label: Banners

sections.body: Explore Novokitezhgrad and Old Kitezhgrad in Snezhnaya, with new Pyro and Geo shotguns, Prime Ice tools, the Ironquill and the Wavebinder boss that drops Mitya's level-up materials.
sections.label: New Area

sections.body: The Grand Defense event lets you help every region against the Hallowing, and you can add a 4-star character of your choice once the threat drops. Ley Line Overflow returns, and Edge of Survival has new stages.
sections.label: Events

sections.body: The Archon Quest gives 560 Primogems and Ascension materials for Mitya if you finish it in time. Exploring the new area gives 400 Primogems.
sections.label: Rewards

sections.body: New Envisaged Echoes for Yae Miko and Xilonen, a new Repertoire of Myriad Melodies album, a Varka card in Genius Invokation TCG, and a Miliastra Wonderland web event starting November 27.
